articles.title: Supremacy of the Constitution
articles.text:
(1) The Sovereignty of Ghana resides in the people of Ghana in whose name and for whose welfare the powers of government are to be exercised in the manner and within the limits laid down in this Constitution.

(2) This Constitution shall be the supreme law of Ghana and any other law found to be inconsistent with any provision of this Constitution shall, to the extent of the inconsistency, be void.

articles.title: Enforcement of the Constitution
articles.text:
(1) A person who alleges that an enactment or anything contained in or done under the authority of that or any other enactment, or any act or omission of any person, is inconsistent with or is in contravention of a provision of this Constitution, may bring an action in the Supreme Court for a declaration to that effect.

(2) The Supreme Court shall, for the purposes of a declaration under clause (1) of this article, make such orders and give such directions as it may consider appropriate for giving effect to the declaration so made.

(3) Any person or group of persons to whom an order or direction is addressed under clause (2) of this article by the Supreme Court, shall duly obey and carry out the terms of the order or direction.

(4) Failure to obey or carry out the terms of an order or direction made or given under clause (2) of this article constitutes a high crime under this Constitution and shall, in the case of the President or the Vice-President, constitute a ground for removal from office under this Constitution.

(5) A person convicted of a high crime under clause (4) of this article shall be liable to imprisonment not exceeding ten years without the option of a fine; and not be eligible for election, or for appointment, to any public office for ten years beginning with the date of the expiration of the term of imprisonment.

articles.title: Defence of the Constitution
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall have no power to enact a law establishing a one-party state.

(2) Any activity of a person or group of persons which suppresses or seeks to suppress the lawful political activity of any other person or any class of persons, or persons generally is unlawful.

(3) Any person who by himself or in concert with others by any violent or other unlawful means, suspends or overthrows or abrogates this Constitution or any part of it, or attempts to do any such act; or aids and abets in any manner any such person; commits the offence of high treason and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to suffer death.

(4) All citizens of Ghana shall have the right and duty at all times to defend this Constitution, and in particular, to resist any person or group of persons seeking to commit any of the acts referred to in clause (3) of this article; and to do all in their power to restore this Constitution after it has been suspended, overthrown, or abrogated.

(5) Any person or group of persons who suppresses or resists the suspension, overthrow or abrogation of this Constitution commits no offence.

(6) Where a person referred to in clause (5) of this article is punished for any act done under that clause, the punishment shall, on the restoration of this Constitution, be taken to be void from the time it was imposed and he shall be taken to be absolved from all liabilities arising out of the punishment.

(7) The Supreme Court shall, on application by or on behalf of a person who has suffered any punishment or loss to which clause (6) of this article relates, award him adequate compensation, which shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund, in respect of any suffering or loss incurred as a result of the punishment.

articles.title: Territories of Ghana
articles.text:
(1) The sovereign State of Ghana is a unitary republic consisting of those territories comprised in the regions which, immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, existed in Ghana, including the territorial sea and the air space.

(2) Parliament may by law provide for the delimitation of the territorial sea, the contiguous zone, the exclusive economic zone and the continental shelf of Ghana.

articles.title: Creation, Alteration or Merger of Regions
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this article, the President may, by constitutional instrument, create a new region; alter the boundaries of a region; or provide for the merger of two or more regions.

(2) If the President, upon a petition being presented to him and, on the advice of the Council of State, is satisfied that there is a substantial demand for the creation of a new region; the alteration of the boundaries of a region; or the merger of any two or more regions; he shall appoint a commission of inquiry to inquire into the demand and to make recommendations.

(3) Where the commission of inquiry appointed under clause (2) of this article recommends in favour of the demand, the President shall, acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State, cause a referendum to be held in the region or regions concerned.

(4) Where the result of the referendum held under clause (3) of this article is in favour of the demand, the President shall create the new region, alter the boundaries or provide for the merger, as the case may be, by a constitutional instrument.

(5) Where a new region is created or regions are merged under this article, Parliament shall by law make provision for the operation and effect of the creation of the new region or the merger, as the case may be.

(6) An issue referred for determination by referendum under this article shall not be taken to be determined by the referendum unless at least fifty per cent of the persons entitled to vote cast their votes at the referendum, and of the votes cast at least eighty per cent were cast in favour of that issue.

articles.title: Citizenship of Ghana
articles.text:
(1) Every person who, on the coming into force of this Constitution, is a citizen of Ghana by law shall continue to be a citizen of Ghana.

(2) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, a person born in or outside Ghana after the coming into force of this Constitution, shall become a citizen of Ghana at the date of his birth if either of his parents or grandparents is or was a citizen of Ghana.

(3) A child of not more than seven years of age found in Ghana whose parents are not known shall be presumed to be a citizen of Ghana by birth.

(4) A child of not more than sixteen years of age neither of whose parents is a citizen of Ghana who is adopted by a citizen of Ghana shall, by virtue of the adoption, be a citizen of Ghana.

articles.title: Persons entitled to be registered as Citizens
articles.text:
(1) A woman married to a man who is a citizen of Ghana or a man married to a woman who is a citizen of Ghana may, upon making an application in the manner prescribed by Parliament, be registered as a citizen of Ghana.

(2) Clause (1) of this article applies also to a person who was married to a person who, but for his or her death, would have continued to be a citizen of Ghana under clause (1) of article 6 of this Constitution.

articles.title: Dual Citizenship
articles.text:
(1) A citizen of Ghana may hold the citizenship of any other country in addition to his citizenship of Ghana.

(2) Without prejudice to article 94(2)(a) of the Constitution, no citizen of Ghana shall qualify to be appointed as a holder of any office specified in this clause if he holds the citizenship of any other country in addition to his citizenship of Ghana: Ambassador or High Commissioner; Secretary to the Cabinet; Chief of Defence Staff or any Service Chief; Inspector-General of Police; Commissioner, Customs, Excise and Preventive Service; Director of Immigration Service; and any office specified by an Act of Parliament.

(3) Where the law of a country requires a person who marries a citizen of that country to renounce the citizenship of his own country by virtue of that marriage, a citizen of Ghana who is deprived of his citizenship of Ghana by virtue of that marriage shall, on the dissolution of that marriage, become a citizen of Ghana.

articles.title: Citizenship Laws by Parliament
articles.text:
(1) Parliament may make provision for the acquisition of citizenship of Ghana by persons who are not eligible to become citizens of Ghana under the provisions of this Constitution.

(2) Except as otherwise provided in article 7 of this Constitution, a person shall not be registered as a citizen of Ghana unless at the time of his application for registration he is able to speak and understand an indigenous language of Ghana.

(3) The High Court may, on an application made for the purpose by the Attorney-General, deprive a person who is a citizen of Ghana, otherwise than by birth, of that citizenship on the ground that the activities of that person are inimical to the security of the State or prejudicial to public morality or the public interest; or that the citizenship was acquired by fraud, misrepresentation or any other improper or irregular practice.

(4) Parliament may make provision by Act of Parliament for the renunciation by any person of his citizenship of Ghana; and the circumstances in which a person may acquire citizenship of Ghana or cease to be a citizen of Ghana.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.text:
(1) A reference in this Chapter to the citizenship of the parent of a person at the time of the birth of that person shall, in relation to a person born after the death of the parent, be construed as a reference to the citizenship of the parent at the time of the parent's death.

(2) For the purposes of clause (1) of this article, where the death occurred before the coming into force of this Constitution, the citizenship that the parent would have had if he or she had died on the coming into force of this Constitution shall be deemed to be his or her citizenship at the time of his or her death.

articles.title: The Laws of Ghana
articles.text:
(1) The laws of Ghana shall comprise this Constitution; enactments made by or under the authority of the Parliament established by this Constitution; any Orders, Rules and Regulations made by any person or authority under a power conferred by this Constitution; the existing law; and the common law.

(2) The common law of Ghana shall comprise the rules of law generally known as the common law, the rules generally known as the doctrines of equity and the rules of customary law including those determined by the Superior Court of Judicature.

(3) For the purposes of this article, 'customary law' means the rules of law which by custom are applicable to particular communities in Ghana.

(4) The existing law shall comprise the written and unwritten laws of Ghana as they existed immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, and any Act, Decree, Law or statutory instrument issued or made before that date, which is to come into force on or after that date.

(5) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the existing law shall not be affected by the coming into force of this Constitution.

(6) Any Orders, Rules and Regulations made by any person or authority under a power conferred by the existing law and which are in force at the coming into force of this Constitution shall, until revoked or otherwise modified by competent authority, continue to apply to those matters to which they applied before the coming into force of this Constitution.

(7) Any Order, Rule or Regulation made by a person or authority under a power conferred by this Constitution or any other law shall be laid before Parliament; be published in the Gazette on the day it is laid before Parliament; and come into force at the expiration of twenty-one sitting days after being so laid unless Parliament, before the expiration of the twenty-one days, annuls the Order, Rule or Regulation by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the members of Parliament.

articles.title: Fundamental Human Rights and Freedoms
articles.text:
(1) The fundamental human rights and freedoms enshrined in this Chapter shall be respected and upheld by the Executive, Legislature and Judiciary and all other organs of government and its agencies and, where applicable to them, by all natural and legal persons in Ghana, and shall be enforceable by the Courts as provided for in this Constitution.

(2) Every person in Ghana, whatever his race, place of origin, political opinion, colour, religion, creed or gender shall be entitled to the fundamental human rights and freedoms of the individual contained in this Chapter but subject to respect for the rights and freedoms of others and for the public interest.

articles.title: Protection of Right to Life
articles.text:
(1) No person shall be deprived of his life intentionally except in the exercise of the execution of a sentence of a court in respect of a criminal offence under the laws of Ghana of which he has been convicted.

(2) A person shall not be held to have deprived another person of his life in contravention of clause (1) of this article if that other person dies as a result of a lawful act of war; or the use of force to such an extent as is reasonably justifiable in the circumstances of the case as is necessary for the defence of any person from violence or for the defence of property; in order to effect a lawful arrest or to prevent the escape of a person lawfully detained; for the purposes of suppressing a riot, insurrection or mutiny; or in order to prevent the commission of a crime by that person.

articles.title: Protection of Personal Liberty
articles.text:
(1) Every person shall be entitled to his personal liberty and no person shall be deprived of his personal liberty except in the following cases and in accordance with procedure permitted by law — in execution of a sentence or order of a court in respect of a criminal offence of which he has been convicted; in execution of an order of a court punishing him for contempt of court; for the purpose of bringing him before a court in execution of an order of a court; upon reasonable suspicion of his having committed or being about to commit a criminal offence under the laws of Ghana; in the case of a person under sixteen years, for the purpose of his education or welfare; in the case of persons suffering from infectious or contagious disease, persons of unsound mind, persons addicted to drugs or alcohol or vagrants, for the purpose of their care or treatment or the protection of the community; and for the purpose of preventing the unlawful entry of that person into Ghana or of effecting the expulsion, extradition or other lawful removal of that person from Ghana.

(2) A person who is arrested, restricted or detained shall be informed immediately, in a language that he understands, of the reasons for his arrest, restriction or detention and of his right to a lawyer of his choice.

(3) A person who is arrested or detained upon reasonable suspicion of his having committed or being about to commit a criminal offence and who is not released shall be brought before a court within forty-eight hours after the arrest or detention.

(4) Where a person arrested or detained under clause (3) of this article is not tried within a reasonable time, then without prejudice to any further proceedings that may be brought against him, he shall be released either unconditionally or upon reasonable conditions, including in particular, conditions reasonably necessary to ensure that he appears at a later date for trial or for proceedings preliminary to trial.

(5) A person who is unlawfully arrested, restricted or detained by any other person shall be entitled to compensation from that other person.

articles.title: Respect for Human Dignity
articles.text:
(1) The dignity of all persons shall be inviolable.

(2) No person shall, whether or not he is arrested, restricted or retained, be subjected to torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

(3) No person shall be required to do forced labour.

(4) For the purposes of clause (3) of this article, 'forced labour' does not include labour required as a result of a sentence or order of a court; any labour required of members of a disciplined force as part of their duties; any communal labour or other civil obligations that is part of the normal civic obligations of the citizens of Ghana; and any labour required during a period of public emergency.

articles.title: Protection from Slavery and Forced Labour
articles.text:
(1) No person shall be held in slavery or servitude.

(2) No person shall be required to perform forced labour.

(3) For the purpose of this article, 'forced labour' does not include labour required as a result of a sentence or order of a court; labour required of members of a disciplined force as part of their duties; labour required of a person while he is lawfully detained which, though not required as a result of the sentence of a court, is reasonably necessary in the interests of hygiene or for the maintenance of the place at which he is detained; any labour required during a period of public emergency or calamity which threatens the life and well-being of the community; and communal labour or other civic obligation of a kind that is part of the normal civic obligations of the citizens of Ghana.

articles.title: Equality and Freedom from Discrimination
articles.text:
(1) All persons shall be equal before the law.

(2) A person shall not be discriminated against on grounds of gender, race, colour, ethnic origin, religion, creed or social or economic status.

(3) For the purposes of this article, 'discriminate' means to give different treatment to different persons attributable only or mainly to their respective descriptions by race, place of origin, political opinions, colour, gender, occupation, religion or creed, whereby persons of one description are subjected to disabilities or restrictions to which persons of another description are not made subject or are granted privileges or advantages which are not granted to persons of another description.

(4) Nothing in this article shall prevent Parliament from enacting laws that are reasonably necessary to provide for the implementation of policies and programmes aimed at redressing social, economic or educational imbalance in the Ghanaian society; or making provisions with respect to adoption, marriage, divorce, burial, devolution of property on death or other matters of personal law; applying or executing any existing law; or imposing restrictions on the acquisition of land by persons who are not citizens of Ghana.

articles.title: Right to Privacy
articles.text:
(1) Every person has the right to privacy and freedom from interference with his private and family life, his home and his correspondence.

(2) No person shall be subjected to interference with the privacy of his home, property, correspondence or communication except in accordance with law and as may be necessary in a free and democratic society for public safety or the economic well-being of the country, for the protection of health or morals, for the prevention of disorder or crime or for the protection of the rights or freedoms of others.

articles.title: Guarantees for a Fair Hearing
articles.text:
(1) A person charged with a criminal offence shall be given a fair hearing within a reasonable time by a court.

(2) A person charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed to be innocent until he is proved or has pleaded guilty.

(3) A person charged with a criminal offence shall be told as soon as reasonably practicable, in a language that he understands and in detail, the nature of the offence charged.

(4) A person charged with a criminal offence shall be given adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence.

(5) A person charged with a criminal offence has the right to defend himself before the court in person or by a lawyer of his choice.

(6) A person charged with a criminal offence shall be afforded facilities to examine, in person or by his lawyer, the witnesses called by the prosecution before the court and to obtain the attendance and carry out the examination of witnesses to testify on his behalf before the court on the same conditions as those applicable to witnesses called by the prosecution.

(7) A person charged with a criminal offence shall have the right to have, without payment, the assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand the language used at the trial.

(8) A person charged with a criminal offence shall not be compelled to give evidence at the trial.

(9) A person shall not be held to be guilty of a criminal offence on account of any act or omission that did not, at the time it took place, constitute an offence.

(10) No penalty shall be imposed for a criminal offence that is severer in degree or description than the maximum penalty that could have been imposed for that offence at the time when it was committed.

(11) No person who shows that he has been tried by a competent court for a criminal offence and has been convicted or acquitted shall again be tried for that offence or for any other criminal offence of which he could have been convicted at the trial for the offence, except upon the order of a superior court in the course of appeal or review proceedings relating to the conviction or acquittal.

(12) Nothing in or done under the authority of any law shall be held to be inconsistent with or in contravention of clause (9) of this article if the law in question imposes upon any person charged with a criminal offence a penalty which is less severe in degree or description than the maximum penalty that could have been imposed for that offence at the time when it was committed.

articles.title: Protection from Deprivation of Property
articles.text:
(1) No property of any description or interest in or right over any property shall be compulsorily taken possession of or acquired by the State unless the following conditions are satisfied: the taking of possession or acquisition is necessary in the interest of defence, public safety, public order, public morality, public health, town and country planning or the development or utilisation of property in such a manner as to promote the public benefit; and the necessity for the acquisition is clearly stated and is such as to provide reasonable justification for causing any hardship that may result to any person who has an interest in or right over the property.

(2) Compulsory acquisition of property by the State shall only be made under a law which makes provision for the prompt payment of fair and adequate compensation.

(3) Any person who has an interest in or right over property which is compulsorily taken possession of or acquired shall have the right to appeal to the High Court for determination of his interest or right, the legality of the taking of possession or acquisition of the property, interest or right, and the amount of compensation to which he is entitled.

(4) Where a compulsory acquisition or taking of possession of property by the State is not necessary for the public interest, the owner of the property, shall recover the property with or without reasonable compensation.

(5) Parliament shall not enact a law which is not generally applicable, which provides for the acquisition of a specific property, or sets out the compensation to be paid for the acquisition of a specific property, unless the acquiring authority reaches prior written agreement with the owner of the property.

(6) Any property compulsorily taken possession of or acquired shall be used only for the purpose for which it was acquired.

(7) Where the property is not used for the purpose for which it was acquired, the owner of the property immediately before the compulsory acquisition, shall be given the first option for acquiring the property and shall, on such reacquisition refund the whole or part of the compensation paid to him as provided for by law or such other amount as is commensurate with the value of the property at the time of the reacquisition.

articles.title: General Fundamental Freedoms
articles.text:
(1) All persons shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression, which shall include freedom of the press and other media; freedom of thought, conscience and belief, which shall include academic freedom; freedom to practice any religion and to manifest such practice; freedom of assembly including freedom to take part in processions and demonstrations; freedom of association, which shall include the freedom to form or join trade unions or other associations, national or international, for the protection of their interest; and freedom of movement which means the right to move freely in Ghana, the right to leave and to enter Ghana and immunity from expulsion from Ghana.

(2) A restriction on a person's freedom of movement by his lawful detention shall not be held to be inconsistent with or in contravention of this article.

(3) All citizens shall have the right and freedom to form political parties and to participate in political activities subject to such qualifications and laws as are necessary in a free and democratic society and are consistent with this Constitution.

(4) Nothing in, or done under the authority of, a law shall be held to be inconsistent with or in contravention of this article to the extent that the law in question makes provision for the imposition of restrictions on the entry into Ghana or the movement within Ghana of a person who is not a citizen of Ghana; the imposition of restrictions on the acquisition or use of land in Ghana by a person who is not a citizen of Ghana; the taking during a period of a state of emergency of measures that are reasonably justifiable for the purpose of dealing with the situation that exists during that period; the imposition of restrictions on the freedom of movement of a person who has been sentenced by a court, or restrictions on the freedom of movement of a person in connection with the enforcement of such an order as is referred to in clause (1) of article 14 of this Constitution; the imposition of restrictions on the freedom of association for the protection of the public interest; or the imposition of restrictions on the freedom of movement of a person who is not a citizen of Ghana, for the protection of the public interest.

articles.title: Rights of Spouses
articles.text:
(1) A spouse shall not be deprived of a reasonable provision out of the estate of a spouse whether or not the spouse died having made a will.

(2) Parliament shall, as soon as practicable after the coming into force of this Constitution, enact legislation regulating the property rights of spouses.

(3) With a view to achieving the full realisation of the rights referred to in clause (2) of this article, the spouse of a person shall be entitled to a fair share of that person's estate on dissolution of marriage or on the death of that person, subject to any other just claims upon the estate.

articles.title: Administrative Justice
articles.text: Administrative bodies and administrative officials shall act fairly and reasonably and comply with the requirements imposed on them by law and persons aggrieved by the exercise of such acts and decisions shall have the right to seek redress before a court or other tribunal.

articles.title: Economic Rights
articles.text:
(1) Every person has the right to work under satisfactory, safe and healthy conditions, and shall receive equal pay for equal work without distinction of any kind.

(2) Every worker shall be assured of rest, leisure and reasonable limitation of working hours and period of holidays with pay, as well as remuneration for public holidays.

(3) Every person has the right to form or join a trade union of his choice for the promotion and protection of his economic and social interests.

(4) Restrictions shall not be placed on the exercise of the right conferred by clause (3) of this article except restrictions prescribed by law and reasonably necessary in the interest of national security or public order or for the protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

articles.title: Educational Rights
articles.text:
(1) All persons shall have the right to equal educational opportunities and facilities and with a view to achieving the full realisation of that right — basic education shall be free, compulsory and available to all; secondary education in its different forms, including technical and vocational education, shall be made generally available and accessible to all by every appropriate means, and in particular, by the progressive introduction of free education; higher education shall be made equally accessible to all, on the basis of capacity, by every appropriate means, and in particular, by progressive introduction of free education; functional literacy shall be encouraged or intensified as far as possible; and the development of a system of schools with adequate facilities at all levels shall be actively pursued.

(2) Every person has the right, at his own expense, to establish and maintain a private school or schools at all levels and of such categories as may be provided for by law.

articles.title: Cultural Rights and Practices
articles.text:
(1) Every person is entitled to enjoy, practise, profess, maintain and promote any culture, language, tradition or religion subject to the provisions of this Constitution.

(2) All customary practices which dehumanise or are injurious to the physical and mental well-being of a person are prohibited.

articles.title: Rights of Women
articles.text:
(1) Women shall be guaranteed equal rights to training and promotion without any impediments from any person.

(2) The State shall provide for maternity protection for working mothers.

(3) Parliament shall enact appropriate laws to ensure that social customs and traditions which are injurious to women or which degrade them or that prevent them from enjoying the full benefits of development are abolished.

articles.title: Rights of the Child
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall enact such legislation as is necessary to ensure that the protection and promotion of all other rights and freedoms conferred on persons in this Chapter are secured against any other person.

(2) Every child has the right to be protected from engaging in work that constitutes a threat to his health, education or development.

(3) A child shall not be subjected to torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

(4) No child shall be deprived by any other person of medical treatment, education or any other social or economic benefit by reason only of religious or other beliefs.

(5) For the purposes of this article, 'child' means a person below the age of eighteen years.

articles.title: Rights of Disabled Persons
articles.text:
(1) Disabled persons have the right to live with their families or with foster parents and to participate in social, creative and recreational activities.

(2) A disabled person shall not be subjected to differential treatment in respect of his residence other than that required by his condition or by the improvement which he may derive from the treatment.

(3) If the stay of a disabled person in a specialised establishment is indispensable, the environment and living conditions there shall be as close as possible to those of the normal life of a person of his age.

(4) Disabled persons shall be protected against all exploitation, all regulations and all treatment of a discriminatory, abusive or degrading nature.

(5) In any judicial proceedings in which a disabled person is a party, the legal procedure applied shall take his physical and mental condition into account.

(6) The State shall ensure the right of disabled persons to education and vocational training.

(7) The State is required to take all appropriate measures to ensure that disabled persons are integrated into the general educational system and that vocational training is provided to enable disabled persons to realise their full potential.

articles.title: Rights of the Sick
articles.text: The State shall ensure that the sick have adequate medical treatment and facilities.

articles.title: Preventive Detention
articles.text:
(1) Nothing in this Chapter shall prevent Parliament from enacting laws that are reasonably required in the interest of defence, public safety, public health or the running of essential services, if those laws are not inconsistent with other provisions of this Constitution.

(2) A law enacted in accordance with clause (1) of this article shall be passed by the votes of at least two-thirds of all the members of Parliament.

(3) A law enacted in accordance with this article shall be published in the Gazette within seven days of its passage by Parliament.

(4) A law passed under this article shall remain in force for a maximum of three months unless it is earlier revoked by Parliament; but Parliament may, on the expiry of that period, extend the law for further periods of three months at a time.

(5) Any person held in custody under a law enacted in accordance with this article shall be released unconditionally or on conditions at the expiration of the period of detention specified in the law.

(6) A person detained under a law enacted in accordance with this article shall, at the earliest opportunity and in any case not later than twenty-four hours after the commencement of the detention, be furnished with a statement in writing specifying in detail the grounds upon which he is detained.

(7) A detainee referred to in clause (6) of this article shall be permitted to consult a lawyer of his own choice as soon as is practicable after he is detained.

(8) Where a person is detained under this article, a tribunal shall be established for the purpose of reviewing, at intervals of not more than one month, the grounds and circumstances of the detention of that person.

(9) A tribunal established under clause (8) of this article shall consist of a chairman, who shall be a Justice of the Superior Court of Judicature or a person qualified to be such a justice, and two other persons, one of whom shall be chosen by the person detained.

(10) Where a tribunal established under clause (8) of this article decides that the detention of a person is not warranted, the person shall be released immediately.

(11) A detainee under this article is entitled to make representations to the tribunal before which his case is reviewed and to be assisted in making those representations.

(12) Nothing in this article shall be construed as authorising the detention of any person by reason of his being suspected of having committed an offence.

articles.title: Asylum
articles.text:
(1) A person who is not a citizen of Ghana but is resident in Ghana has the right to seek asylum in Ghana if that person is being persecuted in his country of origin or the country in which he was last resident.

(2) Parliament shall enact laws to provide for the right of asylum.

articles.title: Enforcement of Fundamental Human Rights and Freedoms
articles.text:
(1) Where a person alleges that a provision of this Chapter has been, or is being or is likely to be contravened in relation to him, then, without prejudice to any other action that is lawfully available, that person may apply to the High Court for redress.

(2) The High Court may, under clause (1) of this article, issue such directions or orders or writs including writs of habeas corpus, certiorari, mandamus, prohibition and quo warranto as it may consider appropriate for the purposes of enforcing or securing the enforcement of any of the provisions on the fundamental human rights and freedoms to the protection of which the person concerned is entitled.

(3) A person aggrieved by a determination of the High Court may appeal to the Court of Appeal and thereafter to the Supreme Court.

(4) The Rules of Court Committee may make rules of court with respect to the practice and procedure of the Superior Courts for the purposes of this article.

(5) The rights, duties, declarations and guarantees relating to the fundamental human rights and freedoms specifically mentioned in this Chapter shall not be regarded as excluding others not specifically mentioned which are considered to be inherent in a democracy and intended to secure the freedom and dignity of man.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.text: For the purposes of this Chapter, 'fundamental human rights and freedoms' includes all rights and freedoms relating to civil and political rights, economic and social rights, and cultural and developmental rights as contained in this Chapter.

chapters.title: The Directive Principles of State Policy

articles.title: Political Objectives
articles.text:
(1) Ghana shall be a democratic state dedicated to the realisation of freedom and justice; and accordingly, sovereignty resides in the people of Ghana from whom Government derives all its powers and authority through this Constitution.

(2) The State shall protect and safeguard the independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ghana and shall seek the well-being of all her citizens.

(3) The State shall promote just and reasonable access by all citizens to public facilities and services in accordance with law.

(4) The State shall cultivate among all Ghanaians respect for fundamental human rights and freedoms and the dignity of the human person.

(5) The State shall actively promote the integration of the peoples of Ghana and prohibit discrimination and prejudice on the grounds of place of origin, circumstances of birth, ethnic origin, gender or religion, creed or other beliefs.

(6) The State shall take appropriate measures to assure as many Ghanaians as possible the opportunity to participate in the decision-making processes at every level in national life and governance.

(7) As far as practicable, every region shall have a fair share of development and social amenities.

(8) The State shall take steps to eradicate corrupt practices and the abuse of power.

articles.title: Economic Objectives
articles.text:
(1) The State shall take all necessary action to ensure that the national economy is managed in such a manner as to maximise the rate of economic development and to secure the maximum welfare, freedom and happiness of every person in Ghana and to provide adequate means of livelihood and suitable employment and public assistance to the needy.

(2) The State shall, in particular, take all necessary steps to establish a sound and healthy economy whose underlying principles shall include the guarantee of a fair and realistic remuneration for production and productivity in order to encourage continued production and higher productivity; affording ample opportunity for individual initiative and creativity in economic activities and fostering an enabling environment for a pronounced role of the private sector in the economy; ensuring that individuals and the private sector bear their fair share of social and national responsibilities including responsibilities to contribute to the overall development of the country; undertaking even and balanced development of all regions and every part of each region of Ghana, and, in particular, improving the conditions of life in the rural areas, and generally, redressing any imbalance in development between the rural and the urban areas; and the recognition that the most secure democracy is the one that assures the basic necessities of life for its people as a fundamental duty.

(3) The State shall take appropriate measures to promote the development of agriculture and industry.

(4) Foreign investment shall be encouraged, taking particular account of the investment policies of the State.

articles.title: Directive Principles
articles.text:
(1) The State shall endeavour to secure and protect a social order founded on the ideals and principles of freedom, equality, justice, probity and accountability as enshrined in Chapter 5 of this Constitution; and in particular, the State shall direct its policy towards ensuring that every citizen has equality of rights, obligations and opportunities before the law.

(2) The State shall enact appropriate laws to assure the protection and promotion of all other rights not specifically mentioned in Chapter 5 of this Constitution which are considered to be inherent in a democracy and intended to secure the freedom and dignity of man.

articles.title: Educational Objectives
articles.text:
(1) The Government shall provide educational facilities at all levels and in all regions of Ghana, and shall, to the greatest extent feasible, make those facilities available to all citizens.

(2) Government shall, to the greatest extent feasible, provide all citizens with the opportunity for continuing education.

(3) Government shall pursue policies which shall seek to eradicate illiteracy and shall, to this end, make provision for the introduction of compulsory basic education of such duration as may be considered appropriate.

(4) Government shall direct its educational policy towards the fulfilment of developmental needs of Ghana and in particular, seek to provide access to educational facilities at all levels in the country.

(5) The State shall integrate appropriate customary values into the fabric of national life through formal and informal education and the conscious introduction of cultural dimensions to relevant aspects of national planning.

(6) The State shall endeavour to preserve and protect the cultural heritage of Ghana.

articles.title: Cultural Objectives
articles.text:
(1) The State shall take steps to encourage the integration of appropriate customary values into the fabric of national life through formal and informal education and the conscious introduction of cultural dimensions to relevant aspects of national planning.

(2) The State shall endeavour to preserve and protect places of historical interest and artefacts.

(3) The State shall take appropriate measures to encourage and support the teaching and use of Ghanaian languages in all its institutions.

(4) The State shall foster the development of Ghanaian languages and culture.

articles.title: Foreign Policy Objectives
articles.text: In its dealings with other nations, the Government shall conduct the foreign policy of Ghana in a manner consistent with the accepted principles of public international law and diplomacy in a manner consistent with the national interest of Ghana and the promotion of African unity.

articles.title: Duties of a Citizen
articles.text: The exercise and enjoyment of rights and freedoms is inseparable from the performance of duties and obligations, and accordingly, it shall be the duty of every citizen to uphold and defend this Constitution and the rule of law; foster the unity and well-being of the Republic; respect the rights, freedoms and legitimate interests of others, and generally to refrain from doing acts detrimental to the welfare of other persons; work conscientiously in his lawfully chosen occupation; protect and preserve public property and expose and combat misuse and waste of public funds and property; contribute to the well-being of the community where that citizen lives; defend Ghana and render national service when necessary; and promote the prestige and good name of Ghana and respect the symbols of the nation.

articles.title: Right to Vote
articles.text: Every citizen of Ghana of eighteen years of age or above and of sound mind has the right to vote and is entitled to be registered as a voter for the purposes of public elections and referenda.

articles.title: Establishment of Electoral Commission
articles.text: (1) There shall be an Electoral Commission which shall consist of a Chairman; two Deputy Chairmen; and four other members.

articles.title: Appointment of Members
articles.text:
(1) The members of the Electoral Commission shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

(2) A person appointed as a member of the Electoral Commission shall not hold any other public office.

(3) A member of the Electoral Commission shall vacate his office if he is removed from office by the President acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State.

articles.title: Functions of the Electoral Commission
articles.text: The Electoral Commission shall have the following functions: to compile the register of voters and revise it at such periods as may be determined by law; to demarcate the electoral boundaries for both national and local government elections; to conduct and supervise all public elections and referenda; to educate the public on the electoral process; to uphold the principle that the will of the people is the basis of the authority of government; and to make regulations, by constitutional instrument, for the effective performance of its functions.

articles.title: Independence of the Electoral Commission
articles.text: Except as provided in this Constitution or in any other law not inconsistent with this Constitution, in the performance of its functions, the Electoral Commission shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority.

articles.title: Demarcation of Electoral Boundaries
articles.text:
(1) Ghana shall be divided into as many constituencies for the purpose of election of members of Parliament as the Electoral Commission may prescribe, and each constituency shall be represented by one member of Parliament.

(2) The Electoral Commission shall review the division of Ghana into constituencies at intervals of not less than seven years, or within twelve months after the publication of the enumeration figures after a census of the population of Ghana, whichever is earlier, and may, as a result, alter the constituencies.

(3) Where the boundaries of a constituency established under this article are altered as a result of a review, the alteration shall come into effect upon the next dissolution of Parliament.

(4) In dividing Ghana into constituencies, the Electoral Commission shall ensure that each constituency has as nearly as possible equal population.

articles.title: Referenda
articles.text:
(1) Where a matter is submitted to a referendum under this Constitution or any other law, the matter shall not be taken to be determined by the referendum unless at least thirty-five percent of the persons entitled to vote at the referendum cast their votes at the referendum.

(2) Where a matter submitted to a referendum under this article is the amendment of an entrenched provision of this Constitution, then, in addition to the requirements of clause (1) of this article, the matter shall not be taken to be approved by the referendum unless at least seventy per cent of the votes cast are in favour of the amendment.

articles.title: Conduct of Elections and Referenda
articles.text:
(1) At any public election or referendum, voting shall be by secret ballot.

(2) Immediately after the close of the poll, the presiding officer shall, in the presence of such of the candidates or their representatives and their polling agents as are present, proceed to count, at that polling station, the ballot papers of that station and record the votes cast in favour of each candidate or question.

(3) The presiding officer, the candidates or their representatives and, in the case of a referendum, the parties contesting and their agents if any, shall then sign a declaration stating the polling station; and the number of votes cast in favour of each candidate or question; and the presiding officer shall, there and then, announce the results of the voting at that polling station before communicating them to the returning officer.

articles.title: Political Parties
articles.text:
(1) Every citizen of Ghana of voting age has the right to establish a political party.

(2) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, every political party shall have a national character and membership shall not be based on ethnic, religious, regional or other sectional divisions.

(3) A political party shall be required to have, as one of its aims, the promotion of national unity and shall not engage in or sanction any form of propaganda that in the opinion of the Electoral Commission has a tendency to arouse hatred, or to cause, or to encourage violence against, any person on grounds of gender, religion, ethnic origin, tribal affiliation or place of origin.

articles.title: Regulations by Electoral Commission
articles.text: The Electoral Commission shall, by constitutional instrument, make regulations for the effective performance of its functions under this Constitution or any other law and in particular, for the registration of voters; the conduct of public elections and referenda; the limitation of election expenses of political parties and candidates; and the compilation, classification and cataloguing of data on the finances of political parties.

articles.title: Parliament
articles.text: There shall be a Parliament of Ghana which shall consist of not less than one hundred and forty elected members.

articles.title: Term of Parliament
articles.text: Each Parliament shall last for four years from the date of the first sitting of Parliament after a general election and shall come to an end on the date before the date of the first sitting of Parliament after the next general election.

articles.title: Qualifications for Membership
articles.text:
(1) A person shall be qualified to be a member of Parliament if he is a citizen of Ghana; has attained the age of twenty-one years; is a registered voter; being a person who was or is a member of the armed forces of Ghana or a Police officer, has resigned his commission or appointment before filing his nomination; has paid all his taxes or has made arrangements satisfactory to the appropriate authority for the payment of his taxes; and is a resident in the constituency for which he stands as a candidate for election to Parliament or has resided there for a total period of not less than five years out of the ten years immediately preceding the election for which he stands, or was born there, or is the nominee of a political party.

(2) A woman shall not be disqualified from standing for election as a member of Parliament by reason only of marriage.

articles.title: Political Parties Representation
articles.text:
(1) Any political party with at least twenty per cent seats in Parliament shall be entitled to an appointment in the Cabinet.

(2) Parliament shall make provision for the implementation of this article.

articles.title: Certain Laws not to Apply to Parliament
articles.text: In the exercise of its legislative function, Parliament shall not enact any law which among other things, shall establish a state religion, provides for the imposition of compulsory labour, provides for the imposition of restrictions on freedom of speech and of the press otherwise than as is necessary in a free democratic society, provides for the acquisition of any property whether that property is the property of the State or the property of a public institution or any other body or person; makes provision specifically or by implication in a manner that is inconsistent with this Constitution.

articles.title: Election of the President
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a President of the Republic of Ghana who shall be the Head of State and Head of Government and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ghana.

(2) The President shall be elected by a majority of all the votes cast at a public election in which every citizen of Ghana of eighteen years and above and of sound mind has the right to vote.

(3) The election of the President shall be held at the same time as the election to Parliament.

(4) A candidate shall not be declared elected as President unless at the voting conducted under this article, the number of votes cast in his favour is more than fifty percent of the total number of valid votes cast at the election.

(5) Where at the voting conducted under clause (1) of this article no candidate is declared elected as President in accordance with clause (4) of this article, a second election shall be held within twenty-one days after the previous election in which the only candidates shall be the two candidates who obtained the highest number of votes at the initial voting and in that second election the candidate who obtains the higher number of votes cast shall be declared elected as President.

(6) In the event of the withdrawal, death or disqualification of one of the two candidates referred to in clause (5) of this article, the candidate who obtains the highest number of votes at the election shall be declared elected as President.

(7) Where the Electoral Commission is satisfied that because of security, natural disaster or other like circumstances affecting free and fair elections in a constituency, election results in that constituency cannot be obtained without exposing voters in that constituency to hardship, the Electoral Commission may, by statutory instrument, postpone the election for that constituency.

articles.title: Executive Authority of Ghana
articles.text:
(1) The executive authority of Ghana shall vest in the President and shall be exercised in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

(2) The executive authority of Ghana shall extend to the execution and maintenance of this Constitution and all laws made under or continued in force by this Constitution.

articles.title: Qualifications for Presidential Election
articles.text: A person shall not be qualified for election as the President of Ghana unless he is a citizen of Ghana by birth; has attained the age of forty years; is a registered voter; and has resided in Ghana for a total period of not less than five years out of the ten years immediately preceding the election.

articles.title: Presidential Term
articles.text:
(1) A person elected as President shall, subject to clause (3) of this article, hold office for a term of four years beginning from the date on which he is inaugurated as President.

(2) A person shall not be elected as President of Ghana more than twice.

(3) The President shall remain in office until his successor is inaugurated.

(4) If the office of President becomes vacant, the Vice-President shall assume that office as President for the unexpired term of office of the President.

(5) In the exercise of the functions of his office, the President shall consult the Council of State on all matters.

articles.title: Presidential Oath
articles.text: A person elected as President shall, before assuming office, take and subscribe to the oath of allegiance and the presidential oath before the Chief Justice or some other judge of the Supreme Court in the presence of the members of Parliament assembled in a meeting for that purpose.

articles.title: Vacancy in the Office of President
articles.text:
(1) The office of President shall become vacant if the holder of the office dies; resigns from office; ceases to be a citizen of Ghana; is removed from office in accordance with article 69 of this Constitution; or vacates the office in accordance with article 66(5) of this Constitution.

(2) A resignation of the office of President shall be in writing addressed to the Speaker of Parliament.

articles.title: Emoluments of the President
articles.text:
(1) The President shall receive such salary, gratuity and other allowances as may be determined by Parliament.

(2) The salary, gratuity and allowances payable to the President shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

(3) The salary, gratuity and other allowances of the President shall not be varied to his disadvantage during his tenure of office.

articles.title: Personal Immunity
articles.text:
(1) Civil or criminal proceedings shall not be instituted or continued against the President or a person holding the office of President in any court or tribunal in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him in his personal capacity before or during his term of office until the expiry of that term of office.

(2) The President shall not be personally liable for the exercise of the powers conferred on him by this Constitution.

articles.title: Vice-President
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Vice-President of Ghana.

(2) The Vice-President shall perform such functions as the President may assign.

(3) Where a person is a candidate in an election for the President, that person shall name his running mate who, if that person is elected as President, shall be the Vice-President.

(4) In the exercise of his functions, the Vice-President shall be subject to the authority of the President.

(5) The Vice-President shall receive such salary and allowances as Parliament may determine which shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Absence of the President
articles.text:
(1) Where the President is absent from Ghana or is otherwise unable to perform his functions, the Vice-President shall perform the functions of the President until the President returns to Ghana or is able to perform his functions.

(2) Where the office of the President is vacant or the President is absent from Ghana or is otherwise unable to perform the functions of his office and the Vice-President is also unable to perform those functions, the Speaker of Parliament shall perform those functions until a new President is elected.

(3) Where the Speaker of Parliament is required to perform the functions of the President under clause (2) of this article, the functions of the Speaker shall be performed by such member of Parliament as Parliament may elect for the purpose.

articles.title: Address to Parliament
articles.text:
(1) The President shall, at the beginning of each session of Parliament, and before a dissolution of Parliament, deliver to Parliament a message on the state of the nation.

(2) The President may, at any time, address Parliament on matters of national importance.

articles.title: Ministerial Appointments
articles.text:
(1) The President shall, acting in consultation with the Council of State, appoint, subject to approval by Parliament, not more than nineteen Ministers of State from among members of Parliament.

(2) A person appointed as a Minister of State shall not hold that office unless that person has been approved by Parliament.

(3) The President may assign to a Minister of State responsibility for any business of the Government of Ghana, including the administration of any department of State.

(4) The President may at any time revoke the appointment of a Minister of State.

articles.title: Removal of President
articles.text:
(1) The President shall be removed from office if he is found, in accordance with the provisions of this article, to have acted in willful violation of the oath of allegiance and the presidential oath; to have conducted himself in a manner bringing the high office of President into ridicule, contempt or disrepute; or to have acted in a manner seriously prejudicial to the interests of Ghana.

(2) Where a notice of a motion to remove the President from office is signed by not less than one-third of all the members of Parliament and is delivered to the Speaker, the Speaker shall act in accordance with the provisions of this article for the purpose of investigating the allegation of misconduct.

(3) Parliament shall, by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the members of Parliament, refer the matter to a tribunal composed of Chief Justice and four other judges of the Supreme Court for investigation.

(4) The tribunal, after due investigation, shall report its findings to Parliament.

(5) Parliament shall, by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all members of Parliament, declare that the President has been removed from office.

articles.title: Appointment of Presidential Staff
articles.text:
(1) The President shall, acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State, appoint the following: the Chief Justice and the other Justices of the Supreme Court; the Chairman and the other members of the Electoral Commission; the Auditor-General; the Commissioner for Human Rights and Administrative Justice and his Deputies; the District Assemblies Common Fund Administrator; the members of the National Media Commission; the members of the National Commission for Civic Education; and such other persons as may be required by this Constitution or any other law.

(2) The President may, acting in consultation with the Council of State, appoint such other persons as may be required by this Constitution or any other law to hold or act in offices the appointment to which is by this Constitution or that other law vested in the President.

articles.title: Determination of Emoluments
articles.text:
(1) The salaries and allowances payable, and the facilities and privileges available, to the President, the Vice-President, the Chairman of the Council of State, the Speaker and Deputy Speakers of Parliament, Ministers of State, members of Parliament and such other Constitutional office holders as Parliament may determine, shall be determined by the President on the recommendations of a committee of not more than five persons appointed by the President acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State.

(2) The salaries and allowances payable, and the facilities and privileges available to persons referred to in clause (1) of this article and who are not public officers, shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Power of Mercy
articles.text:
(1) The President may, acting in consultation with the Council of State grant to a person convicted of an offence a pardon either free or subject to lawful conditions; grant to a person a respite, either indefinite or for a specified period, from the execution of punishment imposed on that person for an offence; substitute a less severe form of punishment for a punishment imposed on a person for an offence; or remit the whole or a part of a punishment imposed on a person or of a penalty or forfeiture otherwise due to the State on account of any offence.

(2) Where a person is sentenced to death for an offence, a written report of the case from the trial judge or judges, together with such other information derived from the record of the case or elsewhere as may be necessary, shall be submitted to the President.

(3) The power of mercy conferred by this article shall be exercised in accordance with the advice of a committee appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of State.

articles.title: Cabinet
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Cabinet which shall consist of the President, the Vice-President and not fewer than ten and not more than nineteen Ministers of State.

(2) The Cabinet shall assist the President in the determination of the general policy of the Government of Ghana.

(3) The functions, procedures and composition of the Cabinet shall be such as Parliament shall prescribe by law.

(4) The Cabinet shall be collectively responsible to Parliament.

articles.title: Oaths by Ministers
articles.text: A Minister of State shall, before entering upon the duties of his office, take and subscribe to the oath of allegiance and the ministerial oath.

articles.title: Treaties
articles.text:
(1) The President may execute or cause to be executed treaties, agreements or conventions in the name of Ghana.

(2) A treaty, agreement or convention executed by or under the authority of the President shall be subject to ratification by an Act of Parliament or a resolution of Parliament supported by the votes of more than one-half of all the members of Parliament.

articles.title: National Security Council
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a National Security Council which shall be responsible for the protection of national interests and for advising the President on matters of national security.

(2) The National Security Council shall consist of the President; the Vice-President; the Ministers responsible for foreign affairs, defence and the interior; the Chief of Defence Staff; the Inspector-General of Police; the Director of External Intelligence; the Director of Internal Intelligence; the Chief of Staff, Office of the President; and such other persons as the President may determine.

(3) The President shall preside over the National Security Council.

articles.title: Ministerial Responsibility
articles.text:
(1) Ministers of State shall be responsible for the policies, administration and other activities of their Ministries, Departments and Agencies.

(2) A Minister of State shall be accountable to the President and to Parliament for the exercise of his powers and the performance of his functions and for the acts or omissions of the officers in his ministry.

articles.title: Deputy Ministers
articles.text:
(1) The President may, acting in consultation with the Council of State, appoint such number of Deputy Ministers as he may require to assist in the performance of his functions.

(2) A Deputy Minister shall not hold that office unless he has been approved by Parliament.

(3) A person appointed as a Deputy Minister shall, before entering upon the duties of his office, take and subscribe to the oath of allegiance and the ministerial oath.

articles.title: Conduct of Business of Government
articles.text: The President shall, subject to the provisions of this Constitution, provide for the proper organisation, allocation of responsibilities and the co-ordination of the work of the various Ministries, Departments and Agencies of Government.

articles.title: Regulations by the President
articles.text: The President may make such regulations as are necessary for the effective operation of the provisions of this Chapter and for that purpose may constitute and dissolve public offices and bodies and prescribe the functions of those offices and bodies.

articles.title: Absence of Minister
articles.text: Where a Minister of State is unable to perform his functions by reason of absence, illness or any other cause, the President may, by writing under his hand, authorise any other Minister of State to perform those functions.

articles.title: Vote of Censure
articles.text:
(1) Parliament may, by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all members of Parliament, pass a vote of censure against a Minister of State.

(2) A motion for the resolution shall not be moved in Parliament unless notice of the motion has been given at least fourteen days before the meeting at which it is to be moved, the notice is signed by not less than one-third of all the members of Parliament, and on the motion coming before Parliament, the Minister has been given an opportunity to state his case before Parliament.

articles.title: Composition of Parliament
articles.text: Parliament shall consist of not less than one hundred and forty elected members and such other members as may be provided by this Constitution.

articles.title: Speaker of Parliament
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Speaker of Parliament who shall be elected by the members of Parliament from among persons who are members of Parliament or are qualified to be elected as members of Parliament.

(2) There shall be a First Deputy Speaker and a Second Deputy Speaker of Parliament, who shall be elected by the members of Parliament from among themselves.

(3) The Speaker and the Deputy Speakers shall vacate their offices when Parliament is dissolved.

(4) The Speaker shall, before entering upon the duties of his office, take and subscribe to the oath of allegiance and the oath of the Speaker.

articles.title: Clerk and other Officers of Parliament
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Clerk to Parliament and such other officers and employees of Parliament as the Speaker may determine.

(2) The persons referred to in clause (1) of this article shall be appointed by the Parliamentary Service Board acting in accordance with the advice of the Civil Service Council.

articles.title: Parliamentary Service Board
articles.text: (1) There shall be a Parliamentary Service Board which shall consist of the Speaker, as Chairman; the First and Second Deputy Speakers; the Majority and Minority Leaders; and four other members who shall be members of Parliament.

articles.title: Disqualification of Members
articles.text: (1) A member of Parliament shall vacate his seat in Parliament if he is absent, without the permission in writing of the Speaker, from fifteen sittings of Parliament during any period that Parliament has been summoned to meet and continues to meet; he is found guilty of gross misconduct; he is expelled from his party; he is found, by the determination of the Speaker, to have ceased to be a member of the party which sponsored his election to Parliament; or he ceases to be a member of Parliament under article 97 of this Constitution.

articles.title: Functions of Parliament
articles.text:
(1) The legislative power of Ghana shall be vested in Parliament and shall be exercised in accordance with this Constitution.

(2) Parliament shall have power to make laws for Ghana or any part of Ghana.

(3) No person or body other than Parliament shall have power to make provisions having the force of law in Ghana except under authority conferred by Act of Parliament.

(4) Any law made in contravention of clause (3) of this article shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void.

(5) Parliament shall have the right to exercise oversight responsibility over all bodies and officers exercising executive authority.

articles.title: Parliamentary Committees
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall appoint standing committees and such other committees as may be necessary for the effective discharge of its functions.

(2) Standing committees of Parliament shall be as provided for in the Standing Orders of Parliament.

(3) A committee of Parliament shall have power to summon any person to appear before it to give evidence or to produce documents.

(4) A person who having been summoned fails to attend before a committee commits a contempt of Parliament.

articles.title: Meetings of Parliament
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall meet at least three times in each year.

(2) Parliament shall meet in ordinary session for a period not exceeding nine months in each year.

(3) Parliament shall also meet at such other times as the President may summon it.

articles.title: Quorum and Voting
articles.text:
(1) The quorum of Parliament shall be one-third of all the members of Parliament and questions proposed for decision in Parliament shall be determined by the majority of members present and voting, with at least one-half of all the members of Parliament present.

(2) The Speaker shall not vote; but in the case of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to have been determined in the negative.

(3) A member shall be entitled to vote on any question unless otherwise provided in this Constitution.

articles.title: Committees of the Whole House
articles.text: Parliament may resolve itself into a committee of the whole house for the consideration of any bill or any matter.

articles.title: Introduction of Bills
articles.text:
(1) Every bill presented to Parliament shall be introduced by a member of Parliament or by the Government.

(2) A bill introduced by a member of Parliament is a private member's bill.

(3) A bill affecting matters of policy shall not be introduced by a private member unless that member has obtained the prior approval of the appropriate minister.

(4) A public bill introduced by the Government shall be introduced by a Minister of State in Parliament.

articles.title: Disqualification from Membership
articles.text:
(1) A person shall not be qualified to be a member of Parliament if he is a citizen of a country other than Ghana; is found, or is declared to be of unsound mind or is detained as a criminal lunatic under any enactment in force in Ghana; is an undischarged bankrupt under the law of any country; holds or is acting in an office, the functions of which involve any responsibility for, or in connection with the conduct of, an election; has, within the ten years preceding the election, been convicted of any criminal offence by a court of competent jurisdiction and has been sentenced to a term of imprisonment of not less than twelve months without the option of a fine; or has been convicted of high crime under this Constitution or of high treason or treason or of an offence involving the security of the State, fraud, dishonesty or moral turpitude.

(2) A person shall not be qualified to be a member of Parliament if he holds an office of emolument in the service of the State or if he is a member of a disciplined force.

articles.title: Financial Measures
articles.text:
(1) Parliament may provide for the levying of taxes and the imposition of duties.

(2) Parliament may make provision to charge expenditure on the Consolidated Fund or any other public fund of Ghana.

(3) A bill for the imposition of taxes or the appropriation of public revenue shall be introduced only by the Government.

(4) Parliament shall not proceed on any bill involving the imposition or alteration of taxes or the appropriation of public funds unless a minister of the Government has recommended it to Parliament.

articles.title: Financial Bills
articles.text:
(1) A bill to provide appropriations of revenue and other funds for the services of the Government of Ghana for a financial year shall be known as an Appropriation Bill.

(2) Parliament may in each financial year authorise the withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of moneys required to meet expenditure charged on the Fund by virtue of this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Vacation of Seat
articles.text: (1) A member of Parliament shall vacate his seat in Parliament if he is absent, without the permission in writing of the Speaker and he is unable to offer a reasonable explanation for his absence to the Parliamentary Committee on Members Interests; he is disqualified from election as a member of Parliament as specified in article 94; he resigns from membership of Parliament, in writing addressed to the Speaker; he is appointed as a Presidential Nominee to the Cabinet; he is expelled from the political party of which he was a member at the time of his election to Parliament; he leaves the political party of which he was a member at the time of his election to Parliament to join another political party or seeks to remain in Parliament as an independent member; or the Speaker is notified by the political party of which the member of Parliament was a member at the time of his election to Parliament that the member has been expelled from that party on account of a violation of the code of conduct of the party.

articles.title: Recall of Members
articles.text:
(1) A member of Parliament may be recalled by the electorate if the member of Parliament has conducted himself in a manner that brings the office of a member of Parliament into disrepute, is corrupt or is guilty of serious misconduct.

(2) A recall of a member under this article shall be effected by a petition in writing signed by more than fifty per cent of the persons registered as voters in the constituency of that member and shall be done through a referendum conducted in that constituency.

articles.title: Election Petitions
articles.text:
(1) No court other than the High Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine any question whether any person has been validly elected as a member of Parliament or the seat of a member of Parliament has become vacant.

(2) A person who questions the validity of the election of a member of Parliament on the grounds of non-compliance with any provision of this Constitution or any other law relevant to elections shall do so by a petition presented to the High Court within twenty-one days after the declaration of the results of the election in question.

articles.title: Privileges of Members
articles.text:
(1) Civil or criminal proceedings shall not be instituted against a member of Parliament in any court or tribunal for a statement made in, or presented to, Parliament or a committee of Parliament or for the manner in which the member voted in Parliament.

(2) The Speaker may, in the presence of a member of Parliament, require the attendance of that member to give evidence at the bar of Parliament or before a committee of Parliament.

articles.title: Parliamentary Decisions
articles.text:
(1) A question of law or right arising in relation to any proceeding in Parliament shall be determined by the Speaker after consultation with the Attorney-General.

(2) Every bill passed by Parliament shall be authenticated by the Speaker and shall be submitted to the President for his assent.

(3) Where a bill submitted to the President under clause (2) of this article is approved by him, he shall within seven days after the receipt of the bill from the Parliament, sign it and the bill shall become law upon the signature of the President being given.

articles.title: Standing Orders
articles.text: Parliament may make, amend and revoke standing orders for the regulation and orderly conduct of its own proceedings and those of its committees.

articles.title: Committees
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall appoint standing committees and such other committees as may be necessary for the effective discharge of its functions.

(2) The standing committees of Parliament include the following: Appointments Committee; Finance Committee; Foreign Affairs Committee; Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee; Government Assurances Committee; Public Accounts Committee; Privileges Committee; Members Interests Committee; Business Committee; and such other committees as may be determined by the Standing Orders of Parliament.

articles.title: Voting in Parliament
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, every question proposed for determination in Parliament shall be determined by the majority of the members present and voting.

(2) A member shall be entitled to vote on any question before Parliament unless the Constitution or any law otherwise provides.

(3) The Speaker shall not vote; but in the case of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to have been determined in the negative.

articles.title: Questions of Procedure
articles.text: Questions of procedure in Parliament shall be governed by the Standing Orders of Parliament.

articles.title: Mode of Passing Bills
articles.text:
(1) A bill may be introduced in Parliament by a minister of State or a member of Parliament.

(2) Parliament shall give adequate consideration to bills, including consideration by the appropriate committees of Parliament.

(3) A bill which has been read a third time and passed by Parliament shall be presented to the President for assent.

(4) The President shall, within seven days after the presentation to him of a bill, assent to the bill or, acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State, withhold his assent and return the bill to Parliament with a statement of the reasons for the return.

(5) Where the President withholds his assent and returns a bill under clause (4) of this article, Parliament shall reconsider the bill.

(6) Where a bill returned under clause (4) of this article is passed by Parliament by a resolution supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the members of Parliament, the bill shall be presented to the President and the President shall assent to it within thirty days after the presentation.

articles.title: Restrictions on Laws
