articles.text: Parliament shall have no power to pass any law to alter the decision or judgment of any court as between the parties subject to that decision or judgment; to deprive any person retrospectively of vested or acquired rights; or to impose a retrospective penalty.

articles.title: Expenditure Bills
articles.text: (1) Parliament shall not, unless the bill is introduced or the motion is moved by, or on behalf of, the President, proceed upon a bill, including an amendment to a bill, that, in the opinion of the person presiding, makes provision for imposing or increasing a tax, imposing or increasing any charge on public funds or varying or repealing any provision relating to such a charge; or altering any provision made by or under an Act of Parliament with respect to the grant of money.

articles.title: Official Language of Parliament
articles.text: Business in Parliament shall be conducted in the English language.

articles.title: Contempt of Parliament
articles.text: Parliament may punish any person who is guilty of contempt of Parliament.

articles.title: Parliamentary Precincts
articles.text: No member of the security services shall be present in the parliamentary precincts except with the consent of the Speaker.

articles.title: Dissolved Parliament
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall stand dissolved at the expiration of four years from the date of the first sitting of Parliament after any dissolution of Parliament.

(2) A dissolution of Parliament shall not affect any bill or motion or other business pending in Parliament.

(3) No general election shall be held less than forty days before the dissolution of Parliament or in the four months immediately preceding the dissolution of Parliament.

articles.title: The Consolidated Fund
articles.text:
(1) All revenues and other moneys raised or received by or on behalf of the Government of Ghana, not being revenues or other moneys that are payable by or under an Act of Parliament into some other public fund of Ghana established for a specific purpose, shall be paid into and form a Consolidated Fund.

(2) No sum shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except to meet expenditure that is charged on the Fund by this Constitution or by an Act of Parliament or where the issue of that sum has been authorised by an Appropriation Act, a Supplementary Appropriation Act or by an Act passed under article 180 of this Constitution.

articles.title: Establishment of the Judiciary
articles.text: The judicial power of Ghana shall be vested in the Judiciary accordingly, neither the President nor Parliament shall have or be given final judicial power.

articles.title: Independence of the Judiciary
articles.text: In the exercise of the judicial power of Ghana, the Judiciary, in both its judicial and administrative functions, including financial administration, is subject only to this Constitution and shall not be subject to the control or direction of any person or authority.

articles.title: Composition of the Superior Courts
articles.text:
(1) The Superior Courts of Judicature shall consist of a Supreme Court; a Court of Appeal; a High Court and Regional Tribunals.

(2) The Superior Courts shall be superior courts of record.

articles.title: Inferior Courts
articles.text: There shall be such inferior courts as Parliament may by law establish, including Circuit Courts, District Courts and such other courts as Parliament may determine.

articles.title: Supreme Court
articles.text:
(1) The Supreme Court shall consist of the Chief Justice and not less than nine other Justices of the Supreme Court.

(2) The Supreme Court shall be duly constituted for its work by not less than five Justices.

(3) The Chief Justice shall preside at sittings of the Supreme Court, and in the absence of the Chief Justice, the most senior of the Justices of the Supreme Court present at the sitting shall preside.

articles.title: Appointment of Justices
articles.text:
(1) The Chief Justice shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State and with the approval of Parliament.

(2) The other Justices of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Judicial Council, in consultation with the Council of State and with the approval of Parliament.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
articles.text:
(1) The Supreme Court shall be the final court of appeal with jurisdiction throughout Ghana.

(2) The Supreme Court shall have exclusive original jurisdiction in all matters relating to the enforcement or interpretation of this Constitution and any matter arising as to whether an enactment was made in excess of the powers conferred on Parliament or any other authority or person by law or under this Constitution.

(3) Where an issue that relates to the enforcement or interpretation of a provision of this Constitution arises in any proceedings in a court other than the Supreme Court, that court shall stay the proceedings and refer the question of law involved to the Supreme Court for determination; and the court in which the question arose shall dispose of the case in accordance with the decision of the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Review of Decisions of the Supreme Court
articles.text:
(1) The Supreme Court may review any decision made or given by it on such grounds and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by rules of court.

(2) The Supreme Court shall sit to consider any application for review within thirty days of the receipt of that application.

articles.title: The Court of Appeal
articles.text:
(1) The Court of Appeal shall consist of the Chief Justice and not less than ten other Justices of the Court of Appeal.

(2) The Court of Appeal shall be duly constituted by three Justices.

(3) The Court of Appeal shall have jurisdiction throughout Ghana to hear and determine appeals from judgments, decrees or orders of the High Court and Regional Tribunals and such other appellate jurisdiction as may be conferred on it by this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: The High Court
articles.text:
(1) The High Court shall consist of the Chief Justice and not less than twenty other Justices of the High Court.

(2) The High Court shall be constituted by a single Justice or, in such cases as the Chief Justice may direct, by three Justices.

(3) The High Court shall have jurisdiction in all matters and in particular, in civil and criminal matters and such original, appellate and other jurisdiction as may be conferred on it by this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Regional Tribunals
articles.text:
(1) There shall be Regional Tribunals which shall consist of a chairman and other members as Parliament may determine.

(2) Regional Tribunals shall have such jurisdiction and powers as may be conferred on them by law.

articles.title: Qualifications for Appointment as Justice
articles.text:
(1) A person shall not be appointed as a Justice of the Superior Court unless he is of high moral character and proven integrity and is of sound mind.

(2) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as a Justice of the Supreme Court unless he is or has been a Judge of a court of superior record for at least five years; or is a lawyer who has been qualified to practise as a lawyer in Ghana for at least twelve years and has practised as such for periods amounting in the aggregate to not less than twelve years.

(3) A person shall not be qualified to be appointed as a Justice of the Court of Appeal unless he has been a Judge of a court of superior record for at least five years; or has been qualified to practise as a lawyer in Ghana for at least twelve years and has practised as such for periods amounting in the aggregate to not less than twelve years.

articles.title: Tenure of Office of Justices
articles.text:
(1) A Justice of a Superior Court shall hold office until he attains the compulsory retiring age of seventy years.

(2) A Justice of a Superior Court may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President.

(3) The appointment of a Justice of a Superior Court shall not be terminated except in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Independence of the Judiciary
articles.text:
(1) The Chief Justice shall be the Head of the Judiciary and shall be responsible for the administration and supervision of the Judiciary.

(2) The Judiciary shall have jurisdiction in all matters civil and criminal including matters relating to this Constitution, and such other jurisdiction as Parliament may, by law, confer on it.

(3) Neither the President nor Parliament nor any person acting under the authority of the President or Parliament nor any other person whatsoever shall interfere with Justices or judicial officers or other personnel of the Judiciary in the exercise of their judicial functions; and all organs and agencies of the State shall accord to the courts such assistance as the courts may reasonably require to protect the independence, dignity and effectiveness of the courts, subject to this Constitution.

(4) A Justice shall not be liable to any action or suit for any act or omission by him in the exercise of the judicial power.

(5) The salary, allowances, facilities and privileges of a Justice of a Superior Court shall be determined by the President on the recommendation of a committee of not more than five persons appointed by the President, acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State.

articles.title: Removal of Justices
articles.text:
(1) A Justice of a Superior Court shall not be removed from office except for stated misbehaviour or incompetence or on grounds of inability to perform the functions of his office arising from infirmity of body or mind.

(2) A Justice of a Superior Court shall be removed from office by the President acting on the advice of the Judicial Council, concurred in by the Council of State.

(3) Before the advice of the Judicial Council for the removal of a Justice of a Superior Court is given to the President under clause (2) of this article, the matter shall be referred to a committee of the Judicial Council to investigate and make recommendations to the Judicial Council.

articles.title: Remuneration of Justices
articles.text: The salary, allowances and other conditions of service of a Justice of a Superior Court shall not be varied to his disadvantage and shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Judicial Council
articles.text: (1) There shall be a Judicial Council which shall consist of the Chief Justice, as Chairman; the Attorney-General; a Justice of the Supreme Court; a Justice of the Court of Appeal; a Justice of the High Court; a representative of the Regional Tribunals; a representative of the Ghana Bar Association; a representative of the Chairmen of Regional Tribunals; a representative of the Judges of the Circuit Courts; a representative of the District Magistrates; and such other members as may be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

articles.title: Powers and Functions of the Judicial Council
articles.text:
(1) The Judicial Council shall, subject to the provisions of this Constitution, have power to make regulations by constitutional instrument or orders with respect to the following: the establishment, changes in designation and abolition of Superior Courts; the granting of leave of absence; the assignment of Justices to Divisions of the Superior Courts; the hearing of appeals from decisions of disciplinary bodies; and all other matters relating to the administration of justice in Ghana.

(2) The Judicial Council shall advise the President on all matters relating to the Judiciary.

articles.title: Rules of Court
articles.text: The Rules of Court Committee shall have power to make and amend rules and orders for regulating the practice and procedure of all courts in Ghana.

articles.title: Reference of Questions to the Supreme Court
articles.text:
(1) The President may, acting in accordance with the advice of the Council of State, refer to the Supreme Court for its opinion any question of law which has arisen or is likely to arise and is of public importance.

(2) The Supreme Court shall pronounce its opinion on a question referred to it under this article in open court as soon as practicable after the reference and that opinion shall, subject to clause (3) of this article, be binding on all courts and persons.

(3) An opinion given by the Supreme Court under this article shall not be treated as a decision of the Supreme Court and accordingly shall not be subject to review by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Prerogative Writs
articles.text:
(1) The High Court shall have jurisdiction to issue writs or orders in the nature of habeas corpus, certiorari, mandamus, prohibition and quo warranto.

(2) The Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal shall have the same jurisdiction as the High Court in relation to the writs mentioned in clause (1) of this article in cases involving the determination of the civil rights and obligations of a person.

articles.title: Special Provisions Relating to Jurisdiction
articles.text:
(1) The Supreme Court may, for the purposes of hearing and determining any matter within its jurisdiction, sit in two or more divisions.

(2) The Supreme Court shall not, while sitting in two or more divisions, sit in a division with less than three members.

articles.title: Customary Law
articles.text: The rules of customary law shall be applied in proceedings before a court in which customary law is relevant and shall form part of the law of Ghana.

articles.title: Circuit Courts
articles.text: Parliament may by law establish Circuit Courts and other courts below the High Court and may vest in them such jurisdiction as Parliament thinks fit.

articles.title: House of Chiefs
articles.text: The House of Chiefs shall have jurisdiction in causes or matters affecting chieftaincy.

articles.title: Court of Appeal Jurisdiction
articles.text: The Court of Appeal shall have jurisdiction throughout Ghana to hear and determine appeals from judgments, decrees, or orders of the High Court.

articles.title: Regional Tribunals Jurisdiction
articles.text: Regional Tribunals shall have jurisdiction to try such offences and hear such appeals as Parliament may by law prescribe.

articles.title: General Jurisdiction
articles.text: The High Court shall have jurisdiction in all matters and such original, appellate and other jurisdiction as may be conferred on it by this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Trial by Jury
articles.text: In cases in which an accused person may, according to law, be tried before a jury, the court shall, unless the accused otherwise elects, try him before a jury.

articles.title: Special Powers of the Supreme Court
articles.text:
(1) The Supreme Court shall have all the powers of the Court of Appeal and in addition shall have supervisory jurisdiction over all courts and over any adjudicating authority and may, in the exercise of that supervisory jurisdiction, issue such directions, orders or writs including writs or orders in the nature of habeas corpus, certiorari, mandamus, prohibition and quo warranto as it may consider appropriate for the purposes of enforcing or securing the enforcement of its supervisory power.

(2) The power conferred on the Supreme Court by clause (1) of this article shall not be exercised in relation to any decision which under any provision of this Constitution or of any other law may be appealed to the Court of Appeal.

articles.title: Appointment of Chief Justice
articles.text:
(1) The Chief Justice shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State and with the approval of Parliament.

(2) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as Chief Justice unless he is a person of high moral character and proven integrity, and has been qualified to practise as a lawyer in Ghana for a period of not less than fifteen years.

(3) A person appointed as Chief Justice shall, before entering upon the duties of that office, take and subscribe to the oath of allegiance and the judicial oath.

articles.title: Vacation of Office
articles.text:
(1) A Justice of a Superior Court shall vacate his office on attaining the age of seventy years.

(2) A Justice of a Superior Court may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President.

(3) A Justice of a Superior Court may be removed from office in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Removal of Justices — Procedure
articles.text:
(1) A Justice of a Superior Court of Judicature shall not be removed from office except for stated misbehaviour or incompetence or on grounds of inability to perform the functions of his office arising from infirmity of body or mind.

(2) A Justice of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice, shall be removed from office by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State supported by a resolution of Parliament.

(3) A petition for the removal of a Justice under this article shall be addressed to the Chief Justice if it is a petition for the removal of a Justice other than the Chief Justice; and to the President if it is a petition for the removal of the Chief Justice.

(4) The petition shall be referred to a committee consisting of a person who holds or has held office as a Justice of a court having unlimited original jurisdiction in civil and criminal matters in a country in which the common law is in force, as chairman; and two other persons who are not members of the executive or legislature or the legal profession, as members.

(5) The committee shall investigate the complaint made in the petition and recommend to the Judicial Council whether the Justice should be removed from office.

(6) The Judicial Council shall, after considering the recommendations of the committee, advise the President accordingly.

articles.title: Local Government Authority
articles.text:
(1) There shall be established in each district a District Assembly which shall be the highest political authority in the district and shall have deliberative, legislative and executive powers.

(2) Parliament shall by law prescribe the composition of District Assemblies.

articles.title: Functions of District Assemblies
articles.text: (1) The functions of a District Assembly shall include the responsible overall development of the district; formulating and executing plans, programmes and strategies for the effective mobilisation of the resources necessary for the overall development of the district; promoting and supporting productive activity and social development in the district and removing any obstacles to initiative and development; initiation, sponsoring and carrying out such studies as may be necessary for the performance of any of the functions conferred by this Constitution or any other enactment; and performing such other functions as may be provided by law.

articles.title: District Level Elections
articles.text: (1) District assemblies shall be composed of two categories of members; the first being elected members, the majority of whom, not being less than seventy percent, shall be elected from the units of the district in a democratic manner through universal adult suffrage; and the second being other members appointed by the President, who shall constitute not more than thirty per cent of all members of the District Assembly.

articles.title: Presiding Member
articles.text:
(1) Each District Assembly shall have a Presiding Member who shall be elected by the members of the District Assembly from among their number at the first meeting of the Assembly held after a general election of members of District Assemblies.

(2) The Presiding Member shall perform such functions as Parliament may prescribe.

articles.title: District Chief Executive
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a District Chief Executive for each district who shall be appointed by the President with the prior approval of not less than two-thirds majority of members of the Assembly present and voting at a meeting.

(2) The District Chief Executive shall be the Chief Executive of the District Assembly and responsible for the execution of approved plans and programmes.

(3) The District Chief Executive shall also be the Chief Representative of the Central Government in the district.

articles.title: Sub-district Structures
articles.text:
(1) There shall be established in each district such number of Sub-district Structures as the District Assembly may determine.

(2) Subject to the provisions of any Act of Parliament, the District Assembly may assign, with or without conditions, any of its functions under clause (1) of article 148 of this Constitution to any sub-district structure.

articles.title: Urban, Town and Area Councils
articles.text: There shall be established in each district such Urban, Town and Area Councils as may be prescribed by law.

articles.title: Unit Committees
articles.text: There shall be established in each district such Unit Committees for the lowest administrative units as Parliament may by law prescribe.

articles.title: Regulations
articles.text: Parliament may make laws, and the Minister responsible for local government may make regulations, necessary to give effect to the provisions of this Chapter.

articles.title: District Assembly Common Fund
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a fund to be known as the District Assemblies Common Fund.

(2) Parliament shall annually make provision for the allocation of not less than five per cent of the total revenues of Ghana to the District Assemblies for development.

(3) The amount standing to the credit of the District Assemblies Common Fund shall be distributed among all District Assemblies on the basis of a formula approved by Parliament.

articles.title: District Assemblies Common Fund Administrator
articles.text:
(1) There shall be an Administrator of the District Assemblies Common Fund who shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Public Services Commission.

(2) The Administrator shall be responsible for the administration of the District Assemblies Common Fund.

articles.title: Accountability of District Assemblies
articles.text: A District Assembly shall be accountable to the people in the district and shall submit an annual report of its activities to the Regional Coordinating Council.

articles.title: Regional Coordinating Councils
articles.text:
(1) There shall be established a Regional Coordinating Council for each region of Ghana.

(2) The Regional Coordinating Council shall consist of the Regional Minister, as Chairman; the Deputy Regional Ministers; the Paramount Chiefs or their representatives; the presiding members of each District Assembly in the region; and the District Chief Executives in the region.

(3) The Regional Coordinating Council shall coordinate, integrate and harmonise the execution of programmes and the provision of services within the region and evaluate the performance of the District Assemblies within the region.

articles.title: Regional Minister
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Regional Minister for each region of Ghana.

(2) The Regional Minister shall be appointed by the President with the prior approval of Parliament.

(3) The Regional Minister shall be responsible for the coordination of the activities of the Central Government in the region.

articles.title: Chieftaincy
articles.text:
(1) The institution of chieftaincy, together with its traditional councils as established by customary law and usage, is hereby guaranteed.

(2) Parliament shall have no power to enact any law which abolishes or creates a superior position to or confers any power on any person or authority to abolish, the office of chief.

articles.title: National House of Chiefs
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a National House of Chiefs.

(2) The National House of Chiefs shall consist of five Paramount Chiefs from each region of Ghana elected by the members of the Regional House of Chiefs of that region.

(3) The National House of Chiefs shall elect a President and other officers from among its members.

articles.title: Regional Houses of Chiefs
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a House of Chiefs for each region of Ghana.

(2) Each Regional House of Chiefs shall consist of the Paramount Chiefs within the region and such other chiefs as Parliament may by law determine.

articles.title: Functions of the National House of Chiefs
articles.text:
(1) The National House of Chiefs shall advise any person or authority charged with any responsibility under this Constitution or any other law on matters relating to or affecting chieftaincy.

(2) The National House of Chiefs shall perform such other functions as may be referred or assigned to it by or under this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Functions of Regional Houses of Chiefs
articles.text:
(1) A Regional House of Chiefs shall perform such functions as may be conferred on it by or under this Constitution or any other law.

(2) A Regional House of Chiefs shall have original jurisdiction in all matters relating to a paramount stool or skin and its occupants in the region; and may also have original jurisdiction in such other matters affecting chieftaincy as may be prescribed by law.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Regional Houses of Chiefs
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the Regional Houses of Chiefs shall be the final authority as far as customs and traditional practices relating to chieftaincy in their respective regions are concerned.

(2) An appeal shall lie from the Regional House of Chiefs to the National House of Chiefs on matters relating to chieftaincy.

articles.title: Prohibition against Participation in Active Politics
articles.text: A chief shall not take part in active party politics, and any chief wishing to do so and seeking election to Parliament shall abdicate his stool or skin.

articles.title: Registration of Customary Laws
articles.text: The National House of Chiefs shall undertake the progressive study, interpretation and codification of customary law with a view to evolving, in appropriate cases, a unified system of rules of customary law, and compiling the customary laws and lines of succession applicable to each stool or skin.

articles.title: Stool Lands
articles.text: All stool lands in Ghana are vested in the appropriate stool on behalf of, and in trust for the subjects of the stool in accordance with customary law and usage.

articles.title: Public Lands
articles.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, all public lands in Ghana shall be vested in the President on behalf of, and in trust for, the people of Ghana.

articles.title: Stool Land Account
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Stool Land Account for each stool into which shall be paid all rents, dues, royalties, revenues or other payments whether in the nature of income or capital from the stool land.

(2) The funds of each stool shall be disbursed as follows: twenty-five percent shall be for the stool through the traditional authority for the maintenance of the stool in keeping with its status; twenty percent shall be for the traditional authority; and fifty-five percent shall be paid to the District Assembly within the area of authority of which the stool lands are situated.

articles.title: Land Commission
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Land Commission which shall have the responsibility for the management of all public lands, on behalf of the Government and the co-ordination of the policies of the Government in relation to land, including the registration of interests in and rights over land.

(2) The Land Commission shall consist of the following members: a Chairman; and not more than six other members.

articles.title: Customary Land Secretariats
articles.text: The government shall provide support and resources as are necessary to enable customary land secretariats to be established for the management of stool, skin, clan and family lands.

articles.title: Taxation of Stool Lands
articles.text: Parliament may impose taxes on stool lands.

articles.title: Compulsory Acquisition
articles.text: Compulsory acquisition of land by the State shall be upon payment of just and adequate compensation according to the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands
articles.text:
(1) There shall be an Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands.

(2) The Administrator of Stool Lands shall be appointed by the President, acting in accordance with the advice of the Public Services Commission.

(3) The Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands shall be responsible for the collection of all revenue accruing from stool lands.

articles.title: Failure of Successors
articles.text: Where in any area of Ghana, there is a failure of successors to hold a stool or skin, the lands previously held by that stool or skin shall vest in the President.

articles.title: Reserved Forests and Protected Areas
articles.text: Parliament shall, by or under an Act of Parliament provide for the reservation or preservation of forests and the protection of the natural environment.

articles.title: Registration of Titles to Land
articles.text: Parliament shall make laws for the registration of titles to land and other interests in or rights over land.

articles.title: Consolidated Fund
articles.text:
(1) All revenues and other moneys raised or received by or on behalf of the Government of Ghana, not being revenues or other moneys that are payable by or under an Act of Parliament into some other public fund of Ghana established for a specific purpose, shall be paid into and form a Consolidated Fund.

(2) No sum shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except to meet expenditure that is charged on the Fund by this Constitution or by an Act of Parliament.

articles.title: Loans and International Business Transactions
articles.text:
(1) Parliament may, by a resolution supported by the votes of a majority of all the members of Parliament, authorise the Government to enter into an agreement for the granting of a loan out of any public fund or public account.

(2) An agreement entered into under clause (1) of this article shall be laid before Parliament and shall not come into operation unless it is approved by a resolution of Parliament.

(3) An international business or economic transaction to which the Government is a party shall not be concluded unless the agreement relating to that transaction has been laid before and approved by Parliament.

articles.title: Contingency Fund
articles.text:
(1) Parliament may make provision for the establishment of a Contingency Fund, moneys from which may be withdrawn to meet expenditure for which no other provision exists, if the President is satisfied that there is an urgent need for the expenditure.

(2) The President shall, as soon as practicable after a withdrawal from the Contingency Fund has been made, lay a supplementary estimate before Parliament for the restoration of the amount of the withdrawal.

articles.title: Public Funds
articles.text:
(1) Parliament shall not impose any tax or levy unless authorised by or under any Act of Parliament.

(2) No money shall be raised for the purposes of the Government of Ghana except in the manner prescribed by or under an Act of Parliament.

articles.title: Accounts and Audit
articles.text:
(1) The public accounts of Ghana and of all public offices, including the courts, the central and local government administrations, of the Universities and public institutions of like nature, of any public corporation or other body or organisation established by an Act of Parliament shall be audited and reported on by the Auditor-General.

(2) For the purposes of audit, the Auditor-General or any person authorised or appointed for the purpose by the Auditor-General shall have access to all books, records, returns and other documents relating or relevant to those accounts.

articles.title: Auditor-General
articles.text:
(1) There shall be an Auditor-General of Ghana who shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

(2) The Auditor-General shall, within six months after the end of the immediately preceding financial year, audit and report on the public accounts of Ghana.

(3) The Auditor-General shall submit his report to Parliament.

articles.title: Independence of Auditor-General
articles.text:
(1) The Auditor-General shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority in the performance of his functions.

(2) The Auditor-General shall examine all public accounts with a view to satisfying himself that the accounts are genuine and that all revenue and other receipts and all issues and expenditures of public moneys and stores are proper and have been applied only for the purpose for which they were appropriated.

articles.title: Powers of the Auditor-General
articles.text:
(1) The Auditor-General shall, in the performance of his functions under this Constitution or under any other law, not be subject to the direction or control of any other person or authority.

(2) The Auditor-General shall disallow any item of expenditure which is contrary to law and shall surcharge the amount of any expenditure disallowed upon the person responsible for incurring or authorising the expenditure.

articles.title: Financial Year
articles.text: The financial year of the Government shall be the calendar year, that is the period of twelve months beginning from the first day of January in each year.

articles.title: Budget
articles.text:
(1) The President shall, in respect of each financial year, cause to be prepared and laid before Parliament, annual estimates of revenue and expenditure of the Government of Ghana for that year.

(2) The annual budget shall include adequate provisions for the service of the public debt.

articles.title: Bank of Ghana
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Bank of Ghana which shall be the central bank and shall be the banker of the Government of Ghana.

(2) The Bank of Ghana shall have the sole right to issue currency in Ghana.

articles.title: Responsibilities of the Bank
articles.text: The Bank of Ghana shall promote and maintain the stability of the currency of Ghana; direct and regulate the credit and financial system of Ghana in the public interest; encourage and promote economic development and the efficient utilisation of the resources of Ghana; and perform such other functions as may be assigned to it by law.

articles.title: Public Debt
articles.text: The public debt of Ghana shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund and every other public fund of Ghana.

articles.title: Appropriation Acts
articles.text: The issue from the Consolidated Fund of all moneys required to meet the expenditure charged on the Fund by this Constitution or by an Act of Parliament, and the provision of the funds required for the implementation of an Appropriation Act, shall be made in accordance with an Appropriation Act.

articles.title: Public Finance Management
articles.text: Parliament shall make laws relating to public finance and may by law delegate to the executive authority in Ghana the power to make provision for any of the purposes for which Parliament may make provision under this Chapter.

articles.title: Parliamentary Oversight of Finance
articles.text: Parliament shall have responsibility to ensure that all revenues and expenditures of the Government are properly accounted for.

articles.title: Remuneration of Auditor-General
articles.text: The remuneration and allowances payable to the Auditor-General shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund and shall not be varied to his disadvantage.

articles.title: Special Audit
articles.text: The Auditor-General may carry out, or cause to be carried out, a special audit of the accounts of any public institution or any institution which receives funding from public funds.

articles.title: Public Services of Ghana
articles.text: (1) The Public Services of Ghana shall include the Civil Service; the Judicial Service; the Audit Service; the Education Service; the Prisons Service; the Parliamentary Service; the Health Service; the Statistical Service; the National Fire Service; the Customs, Excise and Preventive Service; the Immigration Service; the Internal Revenue Service; the Police Service; the Prison Service; and any other service established by this Constitution or by an Act of Parliament.

articles.title: Civil Service
articles.text: (1) The civil service of the Government of Ghana shall be such service as Parliament may by law prescribe.

articles.title: Public Services Commission
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Public Services Commission which shall have such powers and perform such functions relating to personnel management as Parliament may by law prescribe.

(2) The Public Services Commission shall consist of a Chairman and not more than ten other members appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

articles.title: Functions of the Commission
articles.text:
(1) The Public Services Commission shall advise the President on the terms and conditions of service of all public servants.

(2) The Public Services Commission shall advise the President on the appointment of such public officers as are referred to the Commission under this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Police Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Police Service of Ghana.

(2) The Police Service shall be equipped and maintained to perform its traditional role of maintaining law and order.

(3) The Inspector-General of Police shall be appointed by the President acting in accordance with the advice of the Police Council.

(4) The Inspector-General of Police shall be responsible for the operational control and administration of the Police Service.

articles.title: Police Council
articles.text: (1) There shall be a Police Council which shall consist of a Chairman; the Inspector-General of Police; a representative of the Ghana Bar Association; a representative of the Police Service; and other members as Parliament may by law determine.

articles.title: Prison Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Prison Service of Ghana.

(2) The Director-General of Prisons shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Prisons Service Council.

articles.title: Prisons Service Council
articles.text: There shall be a Prisons Service Council whose composition, functions and responsibilities shall be such as Parliament may by law prescribe.

articles.title: Fire Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Fire Service of Ghana.

(2) The Chief Fire Officer shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Fire Service Council.

articles.title: Customs, Excise and Preventive Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Customs, Excise and Preventive Service of Ghana.

(2) The Commissioner of Customs, Excise and Preventive Service shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Board of the Customs, Excise and Preventive Service.

articles.title: Immigration Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be an Immigration Service of Ghana.

(2) The Director of Immigration shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Immigration Service Board.

articles.title: Internal Revenue Service
articles.text:
(1) There shall be an Internal Revenue Service of Ghana.

(2) The Commissioner of Internal Revenue shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Board of the Internal Revenue Service.

articles.title: Security and Intelligence Agencies
articles.text:
(1) There shall be such security and intelligence agencies of Ghana as Parliament may by law establish.

(2) The security and intelligence agencies shall protect the constitutional order of Ghana from subversion and protect the rights of citizens.

articles.title: Conditions of Service
articles.text:
(1) No public officer shall be appointed from outside the Public Service to any public office unless it has been established that no qualified officer is available from within the Public Service for appointment to that office.

(2) An appointment under clause (1) of this article shall not be on better terms and conditions than those applicable to officers in the Public Service who perform similar functions.

articles.title: Protection of Public Officers
articles.text:
(1) No public officer shall, in the performance of his official duties, act on instructions given by any other person or authority except as permitted by or under this Constitution or by any other law.

(2) A public officer who acts otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of clause (1) of this article shall be personally liable for any loss resulting from that act.

articles.title: Civil Service Council
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Civil Service Council consisting of a Chairman; a representative each of the Ministries and Departments of State; and other members as Parliament may prescribe.

(2) The Civil Service Council shall be responsible for the overall management and administration of the Civil Service.

articles.title: Superannuation
articles.text: Parliament shall make provision for the superannuation, pension and gratuity payable to public officers upon retirement.

articles.title: Teaching Service
articles.text: There shall be a Teaching Service which shall be responsible for the management and administration of teachers in the basic and secondary schools.

articles.title: The Armed Forces
articles.text:
(1) There shall be Armed Forces of Ghana which shall consist of the Army, the Navy, the Air Force and such other branches of the Armed Forces as may be established by law.

(2) The primary purpose of the Armed Forces shall be to defend Ghana and protect its territorial integrity and sovereignty.

articles.title: The Commander-in-Chief
articles.text: The President shall be the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ghana.

articles.title: National Security Council
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a National Security Council which shall, under the authority of the President, be responsible for the protection of national interests and for co-ordinating national security.

(2) The National Security Council shall advise the President on matters of national security including the deployment of the Armed Forces.

articles.title: Defence Commission
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Defence Commission which shall advise the President on matters relating to defence.

(2) The Defence Commission shall consist of the President, as Chairman; the Minister responsible for defence; the Chief of Defence Staff; and not more than five other members.

articles.title: Employment of Armed Forces
articles.text: The Armed Forces shall not be employed to act in aid of civil authority except in accordance with an order of the President or under authority of an Act of Parliament.

articles.title: Prohibition against Partisan Activity
articles.text: A member of the Armed Forces on active duty shall not take part in partisan political activities.

articles.title: Service Laws
articles.text: Parliament may make laws governing the Armed Forces and may prescribe the powers and duties of the Commander-in-Chief and the terms of service of members of the Armed Forces.

articles.title: General Legal Framework
articles.text: Except in accordance with an Act of Parliament, the Armed Forces shall not engage in any activities that are not strictly related to their primary purpose of defending the country.

articles.title: State of Emergency
articles.text:
(1) The President may, acting in consultation with the Council of State, by proclamation published in the Gazette, declare a state of emergency in Ghana or in any part of Ghana.

(2) A declaration of a state of emergency shall be approved by Parliament as soon as reasonably practicable.

(3) A declaration of a state of emergency shall not remain in force for more than three months unless Parliament, by resolution supported by a two-thirds majority of all members of Parliament, otherwise provides.

articles.title: Commission of Inquiry
articles.text: The President may appoint a Commission of Inquiry as a matter of urgency during a state of emergency.

articles.title: Offences Relating to Security
articles.text: Parliament shall make laws relating to offences which are prejudicial to national security.

articles.title: Intelligence Agencies
articles.text:
(1) There shall be security and intelligence agencies of Ghana, the establishment of which shall be prescribed by Parliament.

(2) The security and intelligence agencies shall protect the constitutional order of Ghana from subversion and shall protect the rights of citizens.

articles.title: Regional Security Councils
articles.text: There shall be a Regional Security Council for each region of Ghana which shall be responsible for the co-ordination of all security activities in the region.

articles.title: District Security Councils
articles.text: There shall be a District Security Council for each district which shall be responsible for the co-ordination of all security activities in the district.

articles.title: Joint Operations
articles.text: The security agencies shall co-operate with each other and with the Armed Forces in matters of national security.

articles.title: Public Safety
articles.text: All organs of the State shall take steps to protect the safety of the public and to maintain public order.

articles.title: Civil Defence
articles.text: Parliament shall make laws relating to civil defence and may prescribe the powers and duties of civil defence organisations.

articles.title: Commissions of Inquiry
articles.text:
(1) The President may, by constitutional instrument, appoint a Commission of Inquiry to enquire into any matter of public interest.

(2) A Commission of Inquiry shall have the powers, rights and privileges of the High Court or a Justice of the High Court at a trial, for the purposes of requiring the production of documents and the attendance of witnesses before the Commission.

articles.title: Report of Commission
articles.text:
(1) A Commission of Inquiry shall make a full, faithful and impartial inquiry into the matters specified in the instrument appointing it.

(2) A Commission of Inquiry shall, within six months after the last sitting of the Commission, make a report of the result of the inquiry and its recommendations.

(3) The report of a Commission of Inquiry shall be presented to the President.

articles.title: White Paper
articles.text: The President shall, as soon as practicable after the receipt of the report of the Commission of Inquiry, publish a White Paper containing the recommendations of the Commission and the decisions of the Government in respect of the recommendations.

articles.title: Seating of Commission
articles.text: A Commission of Inquiry shall sit in public unless the Commission, for good cause, orders otherwise.

articles.title: Expenses of Commission
articles.text: The expenses of a Commission of Inquiry, including the remuneration of its members, shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Contempt of Commission
articles.text: Any person who fails to attend before a Commission of Inquiry after having been summoned to do so, or refuses to produce any book, paper or document in his power or control, or makes a false statement to the Commission, shall be guilty of contempt of the Commission and liable to punishment in accordance with the rules of court.

articles.title: Legal Representation
articles.text: A person whose interests are, or are likely to be, affected by a Commission of Inquiry shall be entitled to appear before the Commission by legal representation.

chapters.title: Freedom and Independence of the Media

articles.title: Freedom and Independence of the Media
articles.text:
(1) Freedom and independence of the media are hereby guaranteed.

(2) Subject to this Constitution and any other law not inconsistent with this Constitution, there shall be no censorship in Ghana.

(3) There shall be no impediments to the establishment of private press or media; and in particular, there shall be no law requiring any person to obtain a licence as a prerequisite to the establishment or operation of a newspaper, journal or other media for mass communication or information.

articles.title: National Media Commission
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a National Media Commission which shall consist of a Chairman and the following other members: representatives of the Ghana Journalists Association; representatives of the Ghana Independent Broadcasters Association; representatives of the Newspaper Publishers Association of Ghana; representative of the Advertising Association of Ghana; representatives of civil society; and such other persons as Parliament may by law prescribe.

(2) The National Media Commission shall — promote and ensure the freedom and independence of the media for mass communication or information; take all appropriate measures to ensure the establishment and maintenance of the highest journalistic standards in the mass media, including the investigation, mediation and settlement of complaints made against or by the press or other mass media; insulate the State-owned media from governmental control; work to ensure the accountability, efficiency and responsiveness of the public media to the public interest; and receive complaints from and about the media and ensure that such complaints are duly investigated.

articles.title: Independence of the National Media Commission
articles.text: In the performance of its functions, the National Media Commission shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority.

articles.title: State Ownership of Media
articles.text:
(1) The State shall not acquire any interest in or exercise control over any privately-owned newspaper or media of mass communication.

(2) The State-owned media shall afford fair opportunities and facilities for the presentation of divergent views and dissenting opinions.

articles.title: Regulations on the Media
articles.text: Parliament may make laws that are reasonably required in the interest of national security, public order, public morality and for the purposes of protecting the reputations, rights and freedoms of other persons.

articles.title: Editors and Publishers
articles.text: Parliament shall make laws to ensure that every newspaper and other publication circulating in Ghana shall clearly display the name of the editor and the publisher of that newspaper or publication.

articles.title: Media and Elections
articles.text: The State-owned media shall not be used in favour of or against any political party.

articles.title: Commission for Human Rights and Administrative Justice
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Commissioner for Human Rights and Administrative Justice and two Deputies who shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

(2) A person shall not be qualified to be appointed as a Commissioner for Human Rights and Administrative Justice unless he is a person of high moral character and proven integrity and is a lawyer with at least ten years standing at the bar or has held for at least ten years a position of equivalent standing in another relevant profession.

articles.title: Functions of the Commission
articles.text: (1) The Commissioner shall have the following functions: to investigate complaints of violations of fundamental rights and freedoms, injustice, corruption, abuse of power and unfair treatment of any person by a public officer in the exercise of his official duties; to investigate complaints concerning the functioning of the Public Services Commission, the administrative organs of the State, the Armed Forces, the Police Service and the Prisons Service in so far as the complaints relate to the failure to achieve a balanced structuring of those services or equal access by all to the recruitment of those services or fair administration in relation to those services; to take appropriate action to call for the remedying, correction and reversal of instances specified in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this clause through such means as are fair, proper and effective; to seek remedies from the appropriate authorities, and to that end may institute legal proceedings in any court of competent jurisdiction in Ghana in the name of the Commissioner; and to educate the public as to human rights and freedoms by such means as the Commissioner may decide.

articles.title: Independence of the Commission
articles.text: Except as provided in this Constitution or in any other law not inconsistent with this Constitution, in the performance of his functions, the Commissioner shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority.

articles.title: Access to the Commission
articles.text:
(1) A person who alleges that his rights, freedoms or interests have been violated shall have the right to bring a complaint to the Commission.

(2) If the Commission, after making an investigation under this article, considers that the rights, freedoms or interests of the person who made the complaint have been violated, it shall take action to remedy, correct and reverse through negotiation, mediation or other appropriate action the violation.

articles.title: Reports to Parliament
articles.text: The Commissioner shall, not later than the thirty-first day of March in each year, submit an annual report to Parliament on the work done and activities performed by the Commission.

articles.title: Special Report
articles.text: The Commissioner may, at any time, submit to Parliament any special report on any matter which in his opinion is of such urgency or importance that it should not be deferred until the time for submitting the annual report.

articles.title: Remuneration of the Commissioner
articles.text: The salary and allowances payable to the Commissioner shall not be varied to his disadvantage and shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: National Commission for Civic Education
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a National Commission for Civic Education which shall consist of a Chairman and not fewer than six and not more than nine other members.

(2) The members of the National Commission for Civic Education shall be appointed by the President acting on the advice of the Council of State.

(3) The Commission shall create and sustain within the society the awareness of the principles and objectives of this Constitution as the fundamental law of the people of Ghana; educate and encourage the public to defend this Constitution at all times against all forms of abuse and violation; formulate for the consideration of the Government programmes at the national, regional and district levels aimed at realising the objectives of this Constitution; undertake programmes of civic education designed to inculcate in the citizens of Ghana awareness of their civic responsibilities and an appreciation of their rights and obligations as citizens of Ghana; and perform such other functions as Parliament may prescribe.

articles.title: Decentralization
articles.text:
(1) Ghana shall have a system of local government and administration which shall, as far as practicable, be decentralised.

(2) There shall be accordingly established for each administrative unit of the country a governing authority, the prime responsibility of which shall be to initiate and direct the development of that unit.

articles.title: District Assemblies
articles.text:
(1) Ghana shall be divided into districts and there shall be established a District Assembly for each district.

(2) Each District Assembly shall be the highest political and administrative authority in the district.

(3) The District Assembly shall exercise deliberative, legislative and executive functions.

articles.title: Functions of District Assemblies
articles.text:
(1) The District Assembly shall be responsible for the overall development of the district.

(2) The functions of the District Assembly shall include formulating and executing plans, programmes and strategies for the effective mobilisation of the resources necessary for the overall development of the district; promoting and supporting productive activity and social development in the district and removing any obstacles to initiative and development.

articles.title: District Elections
articles.text:
(1) Not less than seventy per cent of the members of a District Assembly shall be elected by universal adult suffrage.

(2) The remaining members of a District Assembly shall be appointed by the President in consultation with traditional authorities and other interest groups in the district.

articles.title: Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies
articles.text: Parliament may, by law, designate any district as a metropolitan, municipal or district area and establish for it a Metropolitan, Municipal or District Assembly.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.text: In this Constitution, unless the context otherwise requires — 'Act of Parliament' means a law enacted by Parliament; 'citizen' means a citizen of Ghana; 'district' means an area designated by constitutional instrument as a district; 'financial year' means the year commencing on the first day of January; 'functions' includes powers and duties; 'Gazette' means the Ghana Gazette or any supplement thereto; 'Ghana' means the Republic of Ghana; 'law' includes any act or statutory instrument; 'member of the security forces' means a member of the armed forces, the police or any body established by law for the defence of Ghana; 'public office' means an office the emoluments attached to which are paid directly from the Consolidated Fund; 'public officer' means a person holding or acting in a public office.

articles.title: Existing Laws
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, all existing law shall continue in force as if enacted, issued or made under this Constitution and shall be construed with such modifications, qualifications, adaptations and exceptions as may be necessary to bring it into conformity with this Constitution.

(2) For the purposes of this article 'existing law' means the law of Ghana as it existed immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution.

articles.title: Existing Offices
articles.text: (1) Where any office is established by this Constitution and a corresponding office existed immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, a person who, immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, held or was acting in the corresponding office shall, except as otherwise provided in this Constitution, be deemed to have been duly appointed to the office established by this Constitution.

articles.title: Transitional Parliament
articles.text:
(1) Until Parliament is duly constituted in accordance with this Constitution, the Parliament in existence immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution shall exercise such legislative functions as are not in conflict with the spirit and the letter of this Constitution.

(2) The provisions of this Constitution which relate to Parliament shall, to the extent that they are applicable, apply to that Parliament.

articles.title: Pending Proceedings
articles.text: All proceedings in any court of law or tribunal pending at the coming into force of this Constitution shall be continued as if commenced under this Constitution.

articles.title: Existing Treaties
articles.text: All treaties, agreements and conventions entered into or ratified by or on behalf of Ghana before the coming into force of this Constitution shall, to the extent that they are consistent with this Constitution, continue to be binding on Ghana.

articles.title: Consequential Amendments
articles.text: Parliament shall, within twelve months of the coming into force of this Constitution, enact such legislation as may be necessary to give effect to all the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Land Administration
articles.text:
(1) All stool lands in Ghana are vested in the appropriate stool on behalf of, and in trust for the subjects of the stool in accordance with customary law and usage.

(2) There shall be established a Lands Commission which shall consist of such persons as Parliament may by law determine.

(3) The Lands Commission shall be responsible for the management of public lands and co-ordinating policy of the government in respect of land, including the registration of interests in and rights over land.

articles.title: Agreements on Natural Resources
articles.text: (1) Any transaction, contract or undertaking involving the grant of a right or concession by or on behalf of any person including the Government of Ghana, to any other person or body of persons howsoever described, for the exploitation of any mineral, water or other natural resource of Ghana made or entered into after the coming into force of this Constitution shall be subject to ratification by Parliament.

articles.title: Minerals Commission
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Minerals Commission which shall be responsible for the regulation and management of the utilisation of the mineral resources of Ghana and the co-ordination and implementation of the policies in relation to them.

(2) The Minerals Commission shall consist of such persons as Parliament may by law prescribe.

articles.title: Petroleum
articles.text:
(1) The entire property in and control of all petroleum in its natural state in, under or upon any land in Ghana, the territorial sea of Ghana or in any continental shelf or exclusive economic zone of Ghana is vested in the President on behalf of, and in trust for the people of Ghana.

(2) The management of natural gas and petroleum shall be regulated by law.

(3) There shall be a Petroleum Commission of Ghana which shall have the responsibility for the regulation and management of the utilisation of petroleum resources of Ghana and the co-ordination and implementation of policies in relation to them.

articles.title: Transitional Provisions
articles.text:
(1) The President of Ghana on the coming into force of this Constitution shall be the person elected as President at the Presidential election held on the third day of November, 1992.

(2) The person referred to in clause (1) of this article shall hold office in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Council of State
articles.text:
(1) There shall be a Council of State which shall counsel the President in the performance of his functions.

(2) The Council of State shall consist of the following members: the former Chief Justice; a former Chief of Defence Staff; a former Inspector-General of Police; eleven other members, one from each region of Ghana, elected by an electoral college at the regional level; one person with physical disability; and the President of the National House of Chiefs.

articles.title: Functions of the Council of State
articles.text:
(1) The Council of State shall consider and advise the President on any matter referred to it by the President, and consider and advise on any matter referred to it by, or under, this Constitution.

(2) The Council of State shall, in the performance of its functions, act with integrity and independence.

articles.title: Meetings of the Council
articles.text: The Council of State shall regulate its own procedure and shall meet as often as necessary for the performance of its functions under this Constitution.

articles.title: Remuneration of Council Members
articles.text: The salaries and allowances of the members of the Council of State shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.title: Entrenched Provisions
articles.text:
(1) This Constitution or a provision of it shall not be amended by an Act of Parliament unless the proposed amendment has been referred to the Council of State; approved at a referendum held for the purpose, in which at least forty percent of the persons entitled to vote cast their votes and the amendment is approved by at least seventy-five percent of the votes cast at the referendum; the proposed amendment has been approved at the referendum; and an Act of Parliament has been passed to give effect to it.

(2) The provisions of this Constitution that shall not be amended other than in the manner referred to in clause (1) of this article are articles 1 to 7; 17; 19; 21; 23; 24; 25; 33 to 35; 41; 42; 43 to 58; 60 to 64; 70 to 78; 80; 83 to 87; 89; 103 to 108; 110; 111; 112 to 116; 125; 127 to 133; 142; 143; 178; 180 to 192; 201 to 213 and 218; and this article.

articles.title: Amendment of Non-Entrenched Provisions
articles.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of article 276 of this Constitution, this Constitution or a provision of it shall not be amended by an Act of Parliament unless the proposed amendment has been supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of all the members of Parliament and submitted to the President for his assent.

articles.title: Commencement
articles.text: This Constitution shall come into force on the seventh day of January, 1993.

articles.title: Citation
articles.text: This Constitution may be cited as the Constitution of the Republic of Ghana, 1992.

articles.title: Schedules
articles.text: The Schedules to this Constitution shall have effect as part of this Constitution.

articles.title: Publication
articles.text: This Constitution shall be published in the Ghana Gazette and be made available to all persons in Ghana.

articles.title: Oath of Allegiance
articles.text: I _____ do solemnly swear/affirm that I will be faithful and bear true allegiance to the Republic of Ghana as by law established, and that I will preserve, protect and defend the Constitution of the Republic of Ghana. (So help me God.)

chapters.title: Code of Conduct for Public Officers

articles.title: Code of Conduct
articles.text:
(1) A public officer shall not put himself in a position where his personal interest conflicts or is likely to conflict with the performance of the functions of his office.

(2) A public officer who is in a position where his personal interest conflicts or is likely to conflict with the performance of the functions of his office shall disclose the nature of his interest to his superior and shall not perform any function in relation to the matter in respect of which he has such interest or is likely to have such interest.

articles.title: Prohibition of Certain Conducts
articles.text:
(1) A public officer shall not use his office to enrich himself or solicit for himself, or for any other person, property, service, promise of service, or other benefit.

(2) A public officer shall not, in the performance of his duties, make any decision in respect of any matter in which he has a personal interest.

(3) A public officer shall not receive any benefit, gift, favour or hospitality from any person other than his employer, in respect of anything done or omitted to be done in the performance of his duties.

articles.title: Submission of Information and Assets Declaration
articles.text:
(1) A public officer shall, before assuming office, submit to the Auditor-General a written declaration of all property or assets owned by, or liabilities owed by, him whether directly or indirectly.

(2) A public officer shall also, at the end of every two years and at the end of his term of office, submit to the Auditor-General a written declaration of all property or assets owned by him, whether directly or indirectly.

(3) A public officer shall not use his office to acquire additional property.

(4) The declaration made under this article shall, on demand, be produced in evidence before a court or other tribunal if it is relevant to any proceedings before the court or tribunal.

articles.title: Declaration of Assets
articles.text:
(1) A person who is appointed or elected to a public office shall, at the time of such appointment or election, submit to the Auditor-General a declaration of all property or assets owned by him, and of all liabilities owed by him, whether directly or indirectly.

(2) A person referred to in clause (1) shall also submit such declaration at the end of every four years and at the end of his term of office, and whenever such person acquires assets or incurs liabilities.

(3) Parliament shall, by law, prescribe the class of persons who shall be required to submit declarations under this article, and the form and content of such declarations.

articles.title: Existing Laws — Adaptation
articles.text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, all existing law shall, on the coming into force of this Constitution, continue in force as if enacted, issued or made under this Constitution and shall be construed with such modifications, qualifications, adaptations and exceptions as may be necessary to bring it into conformity with this Constitution.

(2) Any court or tribunal or person having power to make appointments to public offices may, for the purposes of this article, construe the existing law with such modifications, qualifications, adaptations and exceptions as may be necessary to bring it into conformity with this Constitution.

articles.title: Existing Institutions
articles.text: Where any office is established by this Constitution and a corresponding office existed immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, a person who, immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution, held or was acting in the corresponding office may, if he was in that office by virtue of an appointment, be appointed to the office established by this Constitution, and shall, subject to this Constitution, be deemed to have been so appointed.

articles.title: Transitional Parliament
articles.text:
(1) The Parliament existing immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution shall exercise such legislative functions as are not in conflict with this Constitution until the Parliament constituted in accordance with this Constitution comes into being.

(2) The Speaker of the Parliament referred to in clause (1) of this article shall continue to perform the functions of the Speaker until a Speaker has been elected under this Constitution.

articles.title: The First Parliament
articles.text:
(1) The first Parliament of Ghana under this Constitution shall be constituted as soon as practicable after the coming into force of this Constitution in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

(2) A member of the Parliament referred to in clause (1) of this article shall hold his seat in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Pending Proceedings
articles.text:
(1) All proceedings pending before any court or tribunal immediately before the coming into force of this Constitution shall, on the coming into force of this Constitution, be continued as if commenced under this Constitution.

(2) All proceedings commenced after the coming into force of this Constitution shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Interpretation
articles.text: In this Constitution, unless the context otherwise requires — 'Act of Parliament' means a law enacted by Parliament; 'citizen' means a citizen of Ghana; 'Consolidated Fund' means the fund referred to in article 180 of this Constitution; 'court' means a court of competent jurisdiction in Ghana; 'district' means an area designated by constitutional instrument as a district; 'functions' includes powers and duties; 'Gazette' means the Ghana Gazette or any supplement thereto; 'Ghana' means the Republic of Ghana; 'law' includes any act, statute, statutory instrument, order, by-law, regulation and any other legislative instrument; 'member of the security forces' means a member of the armed forces, the police, the prison service, the fire service, the customs, excise and preventive service, the immigration service or any other public security body established by law; 'Parliament' means the Parliament of Ghana established by this Constitution; 'public office' means an office the emoluments attached to which are paid directly from the Consolidated Fund or directly out of moneys provided by Parliament; 'public officer' means a person who holds a public office; 'sitting days' means days on which Parliament meets in ordinary session.

articles.title: Meaning of Certain Terms
articles.text: For the purposes of this Constitution — a reference to a function shall be construed as including a reference to a power or duty; a reference to the holder of an office by the term designating his office shall be construed as including a reference to any person for the time being lawfully acting in or performing the functions of that office; and words in the masculine gender shall include the feminine gender.

articles.title: Computation of Time
articles.text: In computing time for the purposes of this Constitution — a period of days from the occurrence of an event or the doing of an act or thing shall be computed as exclusive of the day on which the event occurs or the act or thing is done; if the last day of the period is a Sunday or a public holiday, the period shall include the next following day that is not a Sunday or public holiday; and where an act or thing is required to be done within a specified period after or from a specified day, the period begins immediately after that day.

articles.title: Implied Powers
articles.text: Where a power is conferred upon any person or authority to do or enforce the doing of any act or thing, all such powers shall be deemed to be also conferred as are reasonably necessary to enable that person or authority to do or enforce the doing of that act or thing.

articles.title: Exercise of Discretionary Powers
articles.text: Where in this Constitution or in any other law discretionary power is vested in any person or authority — that discretionary power shall be deemed to imply a duty to be fair and candid; the exercise of the discretionary power shall not be arbitrary, capricious or biased either by resentment, prejudice or personal dislike and shall be in accordance with due process of law; and where the person or authority is not a court or other quasi-judicial body, a failure to exercise the discretionary power within a reasonable time shall be deemed to be a refusal to exercise it.

articles.title: Supplementary Provisions
articles.text:
(1) The following provisions shall apply for the purposes of this Constitution. A power to make appointments to a public office shall include the power to reappoint a person formerly appointed to that office and to appoint a person to act in or perform the functions of that office. Where a person is appointed to act in or perform the functions of a public office during the absence or incapacity of the holder of the office, his appointment shall cease when the holder of the office returns to the office or the incapacity ceases.

(2) Where a person is required by this Constitution to take an oath, he may, instead of taking an oath, make an affirmation.

(3) Where a person has vacated an office established by this Constitution, he may, if qualified, be appointed, elected or otherwise selected to hold that office on another occasion.

(4) A reference in this Constitution to power to make appointments includes power to make appointments on promotion and transfer.

articles.title: Gaps in the Constitution
articles.text: It is hereby declared that where on any matter, whether relating to the executive, the legislature or the judiciary or any other matter, adequate provision has not been made in this Constitution, the Supreme Court shall apply such principles and shall take such action as the Supreme Court considers necessary to give force and effect to the intentions of this Constitution.

articles.title: Commencement
articles.text: This Constitution shall come into force on the seventh day of January, 1993.
